The Elder Scrolls only started to find mainstream success between the releases of Morrowind and Oblivion, but Bethesda was keen on expanding the series into a franchise well before that point. The 1997 release of An Elder Scrolls Legend: Battlespire is rarely discussed these days, but it's been hiding a secret for over 29 years. Today, The Strong National Museum of Play has lifted the veil on a mysterious Easter egg that's been lost for decades.

If you're not familiar with Battlespire, it's essentially a linear dungeon crawler set in the world of the Elder Scrolls. It's still a first-person game that retains much of the crunchy RPG combat that defined Arena and Daggerfall, just within a much more constrained location. Battlespire's development was led by the "father of The Elder Scrolls," Julian LeFay, who died in 2025.

As documented on the Unofficial Elder Scrolls Pages wiki, players have known for some time that there's an Easter egg in Battlespire involving a photo featuring a photo of some members of the development team. "It is not currently known how to get this Easter egg to display or if it actually functions in the final game," the UESP wiki laments. However, the mystery has finally been solved thanks to The Strong Museum, which has recently received a set of documents that belonged to LeFay.

On the eve of Bethesda's 40th Anniversary, a sneak peek at The Strong Museum's Julian LeFay papers looks at an Easter egg from An Elder Scrolls Legend: Battlespire that has remained undiscovered for over 29 years.

As explained in a Bluesky video from Strong director Andrew Borman, if you load into the game and hold down the number 1 on your keyboard as you type the word "spire," the dev photo will pop up on screen along with the caption "Battlespire rules!"

The degree to which Battlespire rules is somewhat questionable, since it received mediocre reviews upon release and was jointly credited – alongside Redguard – as the start of a down period for Bethesda that the studio only recovered from with the success of Morrowind. But Battlespire was the final Elder Scrolls game LeFay worked on as a Bethesda employee (though he briefly did contract work on Morrowind) and in many ways marks the final chapter of the series' early format.

The fact that Battlespire still had secrets to reveal after all these years is remarkable, and it's a testament to the lasting impact of the world LeFay ushered into existence that people still care to uncover them.

Todd Howard joins fans mourning "the driving force in the creation of The Elder Scrolls and the foundations of Bethesda as a game studio," Julian LeFay: "Without Julian, we would not be here today"

In a new Q&A vlog on his YouTube channel, Obsidian studio design director Josh Sawyer took a question about why there are so few RPGs in contemporary urban settings. Part of the problem, according to Sawyer: They're more difficult and costly to make than other RPG environments.

"One of the issues as an RPG developer that we've found⁠—at least at Obsidian and Black Isle⁠—is that, compared to a dungeon, generally speaking, a town is four times the expense per square foot, basically. Not really "square foot" but, if you have a map of a given size. If you have a dungeon that's this big, it costs X. If you have a town that's populated with people that feels realistic, that's four times as expensive.

"Obviously, that's a generalization, but that's something that is reflected in our [past] work. As we work on areas over time, when we get towards the end, we realize: 'Holy crap, we spent forever trying to do these maps.'

"For example, at the end of [Pillars of Eternity], we had to do Twin Elms. And that was, one: A big pacing landmine that a lot of people did not appreciate⁠—so, sorry about that. But also, we're back to doing very expensive content. You might ask: 'Well, what's the expense?'

"There's a high density of NPCs, a lot of characters have dialogue. They have their own⁠—maybe not super-unique appearances⁠—but there's just a lot more custom stuff that goes into setting up towns, usually. They're more expensive. Obviously you can do it, though."

Elsewhere in this section, Sawyer cited Baldur's Gate 2's Athkatla, Disco Elysium, and the recent Zero Parades as RPGs that land the plane on believable, dense urban environments⁠—though Sawyer notes that the latter two have the advantage of not needing to work in as many believable combat encounters as other RPGs.

A few others spring to mind for me: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3's version of the titular city. But all of those really highlight Sawyer's point about expense and challenge. Vampire and Cyberpunk were notoriously difficult development cycles for their respective studios. I'll always be a BG3 Act 3 defender, but it's definitely the part of the game with the most noticeable seams.

But even if they're hard to make, I love urban adventures in RPGs, whether as part or the whole of a game. Novigrad and Oxenfurt are two of my favorite parts of The Witcher 3, for example. For a real niche example of an urban RPG you should have on your radar, I highly recommend the early access Moves of the Diamond Hand.

#3814. Dataminer uncovers that Spiny - a character seemingly with no way to operate a car - was meant to be playable in Mario Kart World

A dataminer has uncovered something peculiar in the code of Mario Kart World. Spiny, a tiny little turtle-looking fella with a spiky shell, was meant to be a driver in the game.

This information was discovered by Bluesky user Benial, with Spiny's internal name 'Togezo' listed alongside a selection of other characters. As of writing there's been no model, animation, nor idea of how exactly Spiny would imagine such a feat discovered.

Spiny, for those who don't know, is a menacing creature not particularly known for its driving prowess. 'Spiny' has long been the name for the enemies initially introduced in Super Mario Bros., and has been a staple of the Mario universe since 1985. With that angry look on his face and the spikes lining his shell, one would worry whether it's a good idea to let them behind the wheel at all.

Hey, why not? Boo is a playable driver, and the veteran ghost character also doesn't seem like the driving type. So Spiny may have made a great addition to the roster. Why is it my business whether Spiny has trouble driving a car or not; No one elected me to police the Rainbow Roads.

Mario Kart World is a great racing game that seems to have done well, even without Spiny behind the wheel. The game, as a Nintendo Switch 2 launch title, was present during the console's strong sales last year. The game has since received a selection of updates since its release, including a battle mode and team races to its tour mode.

Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything has been stirring up buzz and earning its fair share of money. However, one honor that had been alluding it was the No. 1 spot at the box office. Well, that's no longer the case, as the doc finally became the top movie in the United States this weekend. And regardless of whether that win can be attributed to people showing up because of all the Oscar buzz, or the scene that literally shows everything, it's also resulted in the documentary obtaining a very rare honor.

It should be mentioned that Fielder's film just barely won the top spot, as Warner Bros. and DC Studios' Clayface just missed winning Halloween weekend after its strong start by a little less than $200,000. Wildwood, which some are calling one of the best and scariest movies of the year, remains in third place this week, while steamy fantasy flick Wicker climbed another spot too. Check out the full breakdown below:

6. BTS World Tour ‘Arirang’ in Buenos Aires and São Paulo Live Viewing

9. The Only Living Pickpocket In New York

The No. 1 spot aside, this is a truly auspicious moment for You Can See Everything, because in a rare turn of events, it's now the fourth documentary ever to win a weekend box office. With that, it now joins Fahrenheit 9/11, Michael Jackson's This Is It and Taylor Swift: The Official Release Of A Showgirl. That's a lineup even more wtf than some of the moments in the film. Nevertheless, this is quite the distinction for Fielder and co.

I Wondered Why Nathan Fielder Was Picked For You Can See Everything. His Answer Confused Me

One way YCSE differentiates itself from this lineup, however, is by having a different path to this milestone. All three of the other movies managed to win the box office in their opening weekends. You Can See Everything opened at No. 2 at the box office weeks ago and held that spot last week before finally grabbing the top spot this week.

Whether Fielder's film will hold that spot again next week remains to be seen. Clayface is still sticking around, and it had about 200 more theaters screening the body horror thriller this weekend. That comic book film is already proving to be a solid win for DC, as it has grossed roughly $83 million worldwide against a reported budget between $30 and $44 million.

Plus, a new month means a new slate of films arriving on the 2026 movie schedule. The Cat in the Hat and Godzilla Minus Zero are among the titles arriving in a week's time, and there's always the chance that they could shake things up at the B.O. next week.

All this to say, I expect You Can See Everything to stick around the Top 10 for at least a few more weeks based on how it's trending. I'm very curious as to just how much longer it'll continue to haul in millions, as I don't know if anyone saw this run coming. I'm just hoping to hear that this means Nathan Fielder is going to get more documentaries in theaters, which I would absolutely love to see.

#3811. Celeste and TowerFall dev explains why both games were suddenly delisted from Xbox

"We did this to support the BDS boycott."

Celeste and TowerFall have both been delisted from Xbox suddenly earlier this week. Per a post on Bluesky, developer Maddy Thorson says this was an intentional move, with the games being removed from sale on Xbox in support of the BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement, which is aimed at protesting various companies linked to, or supporting, Israel's government during the genocide in Palestine.

"For those who're asking, yes we delisted Celeste and TowerFall on Xbox," states Thorson in a BlueSky post. "We did this to support the BDS boycott."

In case you're unaware, Xbox's inclusion on the BDS list is due to Microsoft's partnership with Israel and its prison system, according to BDS itself. The company has provided the country use of its Azure Cloud and AI systems, which have been used consistently over the past few years in the ongoing subjugation of Palestinians. BDS has urged people to cancel their Game Pass subscriptions, boycott leading Xbox franchises - including Call of Duty and Candy Crush - and cease purchases of Microsoft gaming products. As it stands, Celeste and TowerFall are now completely unavailable for purchase within the Xbox ecosystem.

This isn't the first time we've seen developers intentionally opt out of sales on Xbox because of the BDS movement; just a few weeks ago, Big Walk developer House House released a statement noting that its game is not on Xbox because of Microsoft's ties to Israel, and we saw the developer of Tenderfoot Tactics do the same in 2025.

"We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets," noted the Australian developer at the time. "We've made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world, that coordinated collective action can confront even the most powerful interests, and that one day, Palestine will be free."

Microsoft has responded to the BDS boycott previously, acknowledging that it supplied AI technology to Israel's Ministry of Defense, but claims "no evidence" it's been used to "target or harm people in the conflict in Gaza". Various reports, including the one linked above, refute this claim.

Celeste and TowerFall both remain available for purchase on PlayStation, PC, and Switch.

Dragon Age: The Veilguard is one of the more polarizing releases in the beloved RPG series' history despite largely positive reviews, with the writing and story in particular being the most contentious talking point among fans. If former series boss Mark Darrah could point to a reason, and if he carried himself with literally zero humility, he'd probably say it's because he left developer BioWare in 2021 and only served as a freelance consultant on Dragon Age: The Veilguard in the final stretch of development. The fact that he wasn't one of the project leads meant the developers were within their rights to simply ignore his suggestions, and according to Darrah, they frequently did do that.

"There were lots of things that I made recommendations on that were not listened to," Darrah tells Eldorado.gg. "And in fact, in some cases, I would make a recommendation, it was ignored, and then a different group that was also helping would make the same recommendation, and then it was listened to. So it was definitely a frustrating experience for me."

Darrah previously attributed the downfall of Dragon Age to BioWare's preference for "simpler" and "more accessible" RPGs, which he said prevented it from having a major hit like Baldur's Gate 3.

Dragon Age, not to mention Mass Effect and other BioWare franchises, are back in the news following EA's abrupt closure of the studio and cancelation of Mass Effect 5. And before you put the blame on any one game, developer, or team within BioWare, it's worth noting the recently completed $55 billion leveraged buyout of EA by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), private equity firm Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partner.

#3808. Bethesda reportedly revealing The Elder Scrolls 6 next month, and we may know what its subtitle is going to be

Bethesda's hugely anticipated and long-awaited fantasy role-playing game The Elder Scrolls 6 could be revealed "as soon as next month", a new report has claimed - right in the midst of Microsoft's ongoing restructuring efforts.

Per The Verge, this new Elder Scrolls adventure carries the subtitle "Sentinel", which aligns with fan speculation, and the outlet corroborated prior reports that the game takes place within the Tamriel region of Hammerfell. The game reportedly touches on "history of the Elder Scrolls" and will "help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts".

If the game is revealed next month - presumably The Game Awards in early December is a good place for it - it would mark eight years after The Elder Scrolls 6's initial reveal trailer, and 15 years since the release of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim. So, it's certainly been a while, though it's worth noting that The Elder Scrolls: Online has operated all through this period, to give fantasy fans something to bide their time with.

Asha Sharma, CEO of Xbox, said she'd played the game in August on a trip to the Bethesda offices, all while a giant inflatable rat and a union protest took place outside. Indeed, this reveal would take place shortly after Bethesda suffered job cuts - as did many other Microsoft-owned studios - as part of Xbox's "reset".

Xbox has been keen to keep fans optimistic of its prospects during what is undoubtedly a challenging time for the business. Yesterday, Sharma said there was "more demand than consoles available" when addressing a 14 percent dip in Xbox hardware sales. Microsoft's latest 8-K filing - a mandated finance report publicly traded companies have to file to the SEC - states in plain terms that "Xbox hardware revenue decreased 29 percent driven by lower volume of consoles sold".

Sharma has also pointed to the record performances of Minecraft and World of Warcraft: Forever's open beta, and congratulated Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for having its "most acclaimed release in more than a decade". But Xbox's first-party release Gears of War: E-Day reportedly only sold more than 400,000 copies across Xbox and PC, following its day-one Game Pass launch. Analysts speculate that its presence on the service potentially cut into its full-cost sales.

All the while, we're seeing studios decide to not sell their game on Xbox altogether due to the company's presence on the BDS boycott list. Earlier this month, Big Walk's developers declared the game would not come to Xbox because of Microsoft's ties with Israel. And last night, both Celeste and Towerfall were removed from Xbox for the same reason.

So it's safe to say that The Elder Scrolls 6, if it is revealed next month, will arrive into a very different world than the one it poked its head into almost a decade ago. Whether it can help Xbox turn things around: that's the question.

Persona tragics have been begging for remakes of the first two games in the series for ages (at least, the ones who aren't begging for remakes of the PS2-era Shin Megami Tensei games instead). After thoroughly milking Persona 4 and 5, series producer Kazuhisa Wada said in August, "personally, I think it's something we should definitely do."

Now, almost two minutes of footage from what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked via the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit. It shows some dungeon exploration, typically flashy combat, and a dialogue scene all in the modern Persona style.

Oddly, Tatsuya from Persona 2 is one of the party members, though it's possible this is a cross-promotional skin you can equip. Or maybe the remakes will incorporate some kind of Persona Q-style crossover?

While it's fair to be suspicious this could be AI-generated footage, it seems both a bit too long and too internally consistent for that to be the case. And it's not like Atlus hasn't got form, given that we found out the Persona 3 remake was real via a leak as well.

#3805. There are currently "no other Assassin's Creed remakes actively in development", says Ubisoft

Yesterday, Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, and the publisher's comments included quite a big surprise: there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

"One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin’s Creed remake actively in development," Ubisoft said in a statement on its website. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."

This has come as a shock to some players because, back in 2024, Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot specifically mentioned that upcoming remakes - plural - were in active development across Ubisoft studios. "Firstly, players can be excited about some remakes, which will allow us to revisit some of the games we've created in the past and modernise them; there are worlds in some of our older Assassin's Creed games that are still extremely rich," Guillemot said.

Given the success of this year's Black Flag Resynced - which sold over 3.5 million copies and "exceeded annual expectations within its first 14 days" - it's interesting to hear Ubisoft move away from what clearly seemed a popular way of revisiting older games. But it's worth noting that although Ubisoft isn't currently working on remakes, that doesn't mean we won't get them at some point in the future.

"Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back," the company's statement continued. "That door remains open because, after all... Nothing is true, everything is permitted." That last bit, if you're unfamiliar, is a commonly-repeated motto amongst the Assassin Order.

If you're curious about what's next for the franchise, we've got a few ideas. First, there's 'Codename Invictus', which is billed as a "PvP multiplayer Assassin's Creed experience" being led by a team of For Honor veterans at Ubisoft Montreal. The title remains shrouded in mystery, and we've seen nothing of how the game will look or play yet.

Then there's Assassin's Creed Hexe, in development at Ubisoft Montreal. This game is touted as a "darker, narrative-driven" experience that appeared to be aiming for a 16th century European setting when it was announced back in 2022. It was originally believed to be targeting a 2026 release, but earlier this year, Ubisoft head of franchise Jean Guesdon explained the publisher is "taking the time to deliver on its ambitious vision, which means we'll be quiet for a little longer". Following this, a report emerged in August stating that Hexe is still at least a year away.

The Assassin's Creed series remains a pillar of Ubisoft's output, even if the publisher has been enduring a lot of change lately. Late last year, the leader of the Assassin's Creed franchise, Marc-Alexis Côté, left Ubisoft. This coincided with a reorganisation of the company and the creation of the Vantage Studios subsidiary, established by Ubisoft and Tencent, to oversee development of the French publisher's biggest franchises, which includes Assassin's Creed.

#3804. How to collect map fragment at The $.$. Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters mini-season has introduced all kinds of epic scavenger hunts to tackle around the island. One of these hunts is tied to map fragments, with the very first quest you need to tackle asking you to collect a map fragment at The $.$. Rocky.

Even in a mini-season like this one, the island is still pretty large, which means there are lots of places you have to carefully search to find quest items. It’s a fairly daunting task to take on, so if you’re struggling with this one, here’s how to collect a map fragment at The $.$. Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

You can find the map fragment at The $.$. Rocky near the far southern end of this key POI in Fortnite. Specifically, it’s located in a room found on the lower levels of the large ship docked at this location.

To find the map fragment, land at The $.$. Rocky, which can be found near the middle-eastern end of the island. Once you’re there, make your way over to the large grey ship if you didn’t land directly on it.

Head inside the ship, then make your way down to the lower levels. As you’re working on this, you’ll spot a small white diamond icon with an exclamation point in it. This icon marks the precise location of the map fragment found here, so focus on getting closer to it as you descend.

If you’re having trouble finding staircases that lead lower, consider simply breaking the floor beneath you to reach the right spot more quickly. The map fragment can be found sitting near a crate inside a room situated on the lower levels near the southern end of the ship.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Once you find the map fragment located at The $.$. Rocky, walk up to it and hold down the button that appears next to the “Gather the map fragment” text that pops up next to it. As soon as you do, the map fragment will officially be gathered, thus checking off the first step in this larger overarching quest.

In total, there are seven map fragments you must find to fully finish this task. Only one is available to grab each week the season is live, though, so you have to wait and steadily progress to earn them all.

If you’re up for some more exploring and adventuring, there’s plenty more to get done this season. Next, you might consider checking out all Treasure Hunters battle pass skins, trying to access the Pirate Shop, finding Devil Fruits, and solving the Frog Statue puzzle.

I've been a big fan of comedian Grace Reiter since I first saw her on TikTok, and her recent addition to the Saturday Night Live cast has only elevated her star power. I was excited to see she's a part of streaming comedy doing well, as those with a Netflix subscription are finding out about Minimum Wage.

The series follows the young employees of "The Slice Club," a pizza franchise operating across the United States. It all kicks off when Randall Park's Terry Sylvester shows up for an impromptu visit as the company's CEO. I was psyched to see Park in the series and eager to see how the show developed, so I was disappointed when the series largely went on without acknowledging him.

I hadn't gotten enough of Randall Park on the 2026 TV schedule, and I don't have enough of him on Minimum Wage. The pilot sets the stage perfectly with his introduction, and even ends with him moving into the basement of the pizza shop, determined to turn around the lowest-performing store's numbers.

He then proceeds to appear in very little of the series from that point onward. It's baffling considering he is such a television staple, and it almost gives the impression that he was shoehorned into the series at the late stages in order to give Minimum Wage a bit more star power. He never really has as much screen time as he does in the first episode, and most scenes after are only a couple of minutes long.

We have no idea if future seasons of Minimum Wage are part of Netflix's upcoming schedule. If it does return, however, I would humbly request that Randall Park's Terry Sylvester have a larger role in the show than he did in Season 1.

The One Thing Matthew Perry's Sister Loves About The Netflix Documentary Telling Her Brother's Story

To me, the fun in this show is a bunch of teens awkwardly dealing with a middle-aged man experiencing a midlife crisis. While I did enjoy the workplace antics and some of the downsides of serving a room full of theater kids, I feel like the well for content on that can only go so deep.

I do question if Grace Reiter's Saturday Night Live schedule will allow her to continue to commit time to Minimum Wage if it returns for another season. It does seem like more SNL stars than ever are popping up in projects while also doing the show, rather than striking off on their own after a couple of years. I think it has potential, provided they can tweak the series a bit to include more of Randall Park.

Watch Minimum Wage on Netflix right now, as well as all of the other great shows on the platform! I'm still obsessed with The Boroughs despite it being cancelled, and come to think of it, maybe it would've benefitted from having Randall Park involved as well.

#3802. Games industry honours beloved actor Sir Patrick Stewart, as the legendary Star Trek and X-Men actor passes away

"An emperor, a captain, and an inspiration to us all."

As I'm sure you're all now already aware, legendary British actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died, aged 86. His Instagram account announced the news yesterday, saying he died at home in Los Angeles surrounded by friends and family, following "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia".

Stewart, a poised and charming actor, was probably best known for his on-screen roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, and Charles Xavier-slash-Professor X in various X-Men films. But he also enjoyed a long and celebrated career on stage.

Stewart appeared in games, too, most notably in Bethesda's fourth Elder Scrolls game, Oblivion, as Emperor Uriel Septim 7th. He effectively kicked the adventure off, narrating the game's intro with gravitas before appearing as Septim to the player in their prison cell. There, he declared he'd seen the player in his dream and proceeded to let us free.

"I️ was born 87 years ago," Stewart's opening monologue began. "For 65 years I've ruled as Tamriel's emperor. But for all these years I've never been the ruler of my own dreams. I have seen the gates of Oblivion, beyond which no waking eye may see. Behold, in darkness a doom sweeps the land. This is the 27th of Last Seed, the year of Akatosh 433. These are the closing days of the Third Era, and the final hours of my life."

Bethesda, upon hearing of Stewart's passing, posted a picture of Emperor Uriel Septim from the recent Oblivion remaster, alongside the words: "Rest in peace to Sir Patrick Stewart - an emperor, a captain, and an inspiration to us all. Our thoughts are with his loved ones."

Stewart also notably voiced the narrator in both of MercurySteam's Castlevania: Lord of Shadows games, and appeared in a number of X-Men games and Star Trek games, as well as smaller projects like Polish Holocaust game My Memory of Us. In honour of his life and work, The Star Trek Online community gathered in large numbers, arranging spaceships in long lines to mark his passing.

Messages celebrating the person Stewart was have flooded social media overnight, written by the many people he impacted during his life and long career. Long-time X-Men collaborator and Wolverine actor Hugh Jackman said: "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."

And Sir Ian McKellen, the Magneto actor who was considered one of Stewart's best friends, gave an overview of the many years the two had known each other, from being "ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago", to working on X-Men together. McKellen recalled cautioning Stewart about taking the lead role in Star Trek because of the effect it would have on his stage career - advice Stewart fortuitously overrode. McKellen referred to his friend as "the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic".

Rest in peace, Sir Patrick Stewart. There won't be another like you.

#3801. How to get Solid Gold A$AP Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters season is shaping up to be perhaps the most generous season of all time, with loads of free cosmetics up for grabs. One of the rarest and most special items you can get is Solid Gold A$AP Rocky.

Lots of the mechanics featured in this season are unlike anything we’ve seen before, so figuring out how to get your hands on this freebie and others like it can be tricky. To ensure you don’t miss out on this epic prize, here’s how to get Solid Gold A$AP Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

Solid Gold A$AP Rocky is a random treasure chest loot item, which means there’s a chance you might find him while looting anywhere around the Fortnite island. He is not a guaranteed drop at any point, and is one of the rarest items in rotation, so it generally takes a lot of searching and quite a bit of good luck to acquire him.

Anytime you open a treasure chest, you might only find standard loot, or you may instead also be rewarded with some extra special freebies. Solid Gold A$AP Rocky is one of the potential prizes included among the bonus goodies you may find.

All of the potential bonus assets you may find while looting are as follows.

Since there’s a pretty expansive pool of potential bonus items you might find while looting, actually getting Solid Gold A$AP Rocky can be tough, as many of the other possible items have better drop rates than he does. Still, all you can do is loot as much as possible and hope luck favors you.

You’ll know you’ve found Solid Gold A$AP Rocky or another special item from the bonus pool when you get a gold pop-up near the top middle section of the screen. This pop-up will highlight the prize you found, which is then granted to you upon returning to the lobby after the round ends.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Solid Gold A$AP Rocky can potentially be found in any treasure chest around the island. There are no fixed spawn locations for this loot drop, so anytime you find and open a chest while he’s featured in the loot pool, there’s a chance you may unlock him.

Solid Gold A$AP Rocky is available to find in the loot pool from Nov. 1 to Nov. 7. The featured skin switches over to Lil Uzi Vert at 8am CT on Nov. 7, so you have about a week to search for it before it leaves the pool.

After his initial availability period ends, it’s unclear when or if Solid Gold A$AP Rocky will be available to obtain. He could potentially return to the loot pool near the end of the season, may be added as a shop asset you have to buy with V-Bucks, or may be altogether unobtainable once the initial treasure hunt run ends.

Once we know what his availability looks like after his run in the loot pool ends, we’ll provide an update here. If you’re determined to grab him for free, though, it’s a good idea to go hunting for him before Nov. 7, as this is the only guaranteed way to get him for now.

If you’re looking for some tasks to keep you busy while you hunt for Solid Gold A$AP Rocky, there’s plenty to choose from. You might consider collecting a map fragment at The $.$. Rocky, finding Devil Fruits, and checking out all Treasure Hunters battle pass skins.

Avalon Hill's deluxe rerelease of the classic dungeon crawl board game HeroQuest is getting a digital edition courtesy of Nomad Games, who previously adapted board games like Talisman, Love Letter, and Fury of Dracula. Expect goblin-bashing, trap-disarming, treasure-hunting, and spell-casting. I'll use my broadsword.

As well as solo play, with the computer taking on the role of the Evil Wizard and his minions, it'll support online multiplayer with up to four players as the heroes, and a fifth optionally taking over as the villainous Zargon. (It's based on the American version, so no Morcar here.)

The most promising detail revealed so far is the inclusion of a quest editor so players can create their own maps and missions, as well as downloading quests made by others through mod.io integration.

Hopefully it includes the rules additions from HeroQuest First Light, especially the option to just move eight squares per turn instead of rolling to move if there aren't any monsters on the board. Slogging across the dungeon to get back to the exit 2d6 squares at a time is a real chore otherwise.

HeroQuest: Digital Edition is scheduled for release on Steam in 2027, with a closed beta playtest coming soon.

#3798. Sony has snapped up the film rights for Mouthwashing

Sony has snatched up the movie rights for Mouthwashing, the hit independent horror video game released in 2024.

Deadline reports Sony has obtained the rights from developer Wrong Organ and publisher Critical Reflex, and also brought on Karyn Kusama to direct the adaptation, a director perhaps best known for her work on the acclaimed Yellowjackets television show.

Sony has also enlisted Matt Manfredi and Phil Hay to write for the project, as well as production company Crooked Highway (who you may know for the Ethan Hawke–lead series of movies, The Black Phone). There is no word on which actors will star in the adaptation as of yet, nor whether the story will follow that of the game's own narrative.

Mouthwashing was a critically acclaimed release, and sold more than 500,000 copies as of February 2025. That was on PC alone, with the game made available on consoles yesterday.

This adaptation would arguably follow the path paved by the Iron Lung movie, created by Mark Fischbach (better known by his online alias Markiplier) and his own production company Markiplier Studios. That, a film adaptation of an indie horror game, performed exceptionally well at the box office bringing in $21m globally shortly after its premiere.

A Mouthwashing movie is an interesting idea. The main question is whether or not it would follow the plot and narrative structure of the game faithfully, or whether changes would be made to better suit the big screen. A sillier - but awfully tantalising - question, is who you'd like to see casted in the movie? Who'd play Swansea… Who'd play Jimmy?!? Questions abound.

Rosario Dawson and Hayden Christensen know exactly how to get Star Wars fans worked up. Put them together, add a little Anakin-and-Ahsoka nostalgia, and people are already paying attention. Wrap both actors in sheer blue fabric so they look suspiciously like Force ghosts, and suddenly everyone starts wondering whether Dave Filoni is trying to tell us something about an upcoming movie release or another new Star Wars project. That is exactly what happened after Dawson shared a photo with Christensen that put a very funny spin on their Ahsoka connection.

In an Instagram post, the two Star Wars mainstays are not actually dressed as Ahsoka Tano and Anakin Skywalker. Christensen appears to be wearing regular clothes under a layer of translucent blue layer, while Dawson wears what looks more like a medieval or fantasy costume. If anything, the dress gives off a little Princess Fiona energy. See for yourself in her post below:

A post shared by rosariodawson (@rosariodawson)

Dawson made the joke even more obvious with her caption: “MAY THE FORCE GHOSTS BE WITH YOU 👻👻.”

The costumes are goofy, simple and immediately recognizable. Christensen looking like a Force ghost is also perfectly reasonable within Star Wars movie canon. Dawson getting the same treatment, however, is where fans started getting nervous. Because, uh… Why is Rosario Dawson a Force ghost?

To be clear, nobody at Lucasfilm announced the death of Ahsoka Tano's death through an Instagram costume photo. Dawson is not dressed as Ahsoka here, and there is no reason to think she casually spoiled one of the biggest possible developments in Ahsoka Season 2. That didn't stop fans from noticing the implication and asking a ton of questions.

Comments under the Clerks 2 actress's post quickly filled with people who remembered that becoming a Force ghost usually requires a fairly serious prerequisite. Fans wrote:

I understand the reaction. Ahsoka has survived Order 66, Darth Vader, the World Between Worlds and enough lightsaber fights to make most Jedi reconsider the profession entirely. She has also spent years bouncing between animated and live-action Star Wars, becoming one of the franchise's most durable characters in the process.

Christensen as a Jedi specter has precedent. Anakin appeared as a Force ghost at the end of Ahsoka Season 1, and the original trilogy was later reworked to insert the actor into the old footage. Christensen is also returning for Season 2, with Anakin expected to remain part of Tano's story.

Dawson's Ahsoka, meanwhile, is still very much alive when Season 2 begins. She and Sabine Wren remain stranded beyond the known galaxy while Grand Admiral Thrawn has returned home and prepares for whatever comes next. So when the actress playing her suddenly appears next to Anakin's actor, both covered in ghostly blue fabric, fans will read into it.

For now, though, I am choosing the much less stressful explanation. They found some blue fabric, put it over their heads, and somebody took a photo. Nobody is dying. Probably.

Season 2 of Ahsoka hits the streaming calendar on January 20, 2027, for everyone with a Disney+ subscription. Fans can also stream all of the Star Wars movies -- including the prequels featuring Hayden Christensen -- using that same membership.

#3796. How to use Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

In Fortnite Treasure Hunters, there are lots of special, seasonal Sprites waiting to be found around the island. One of the first quests you’ll encounter tasks you with using Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests.

The process for acquiring Sprites changes a bit each season, and this task is quite unlike anything we’ve seen before, so it can be a bit tricky to navigate at first. If you’re struggling to get through it, here’s how to use Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests in Fortnite.

You can find Sprite Wanted Posters hanging up on walls anywhere around the Fortnite island. They’re marked with a special symbol and glow color different from the ones used for chests, which makes locating them a bit easier.

Sprite Wanted Posters are marked with a square, poster-shaped icon that has a question mark on it. The glow for these special posters is a softer, slightly lighter gold shade than the one that marks regular chests.

All Wanted Posters are consumables, which means only one player can find and use each one, as they turn into a Sprite Treasure Map you can use as soon as you interact with them. Because of this, they’re more common earlier on in each round.

To complete the use Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests, you need to find and interact with three Wanted Posters, pick up the Sprite Treasure Map that drops from each one, and use it to find and open a Sprite Chest. #3795. Forza director, who'd been with Turn 10 for 27 years leaves Microsoft, following studios merger with Playground Games

Dan Greenawalt, director, founder, and vice president at Turn 10 Games, has departed from the studio after spending 27 years as part of the company. This comes as Turn 10 is merged with Playground Games as part of Xbox's mass restructuring initiative that made headlines as it resulted in 3200 layoffs and four studio closures earlier this year.

In a report by The Verge, an internal memo written by Playground Games studio head Trevor Williams states: "Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft".

The memo continues: "It's hard to overstate Dan's impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original Xbox in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow – and so much more – we owe tremendous thanks and gratitude to Dan. On behalf of both teams, I would like to thank Dan for his leadership, his support, and his partnership. I wish him well for whatever comes next.".

With Xbox's merger of Playground Games and Turn 10, the developers will be working in collaboration on the Forza and Fable franchises. The final track racer game that Playground Games developed prior to this merger was 2023's Forza Motorsport reboot, a wonderful racer that offered a sweet alternative to the more arcade Forza Horizon series. In Eurogamer's review, the game was described as: "A generous and lavish racer, with thrilling driving, that wants you for the long haul.".

#3794. Team Behind Fan-Made Oblivion Remake Face Lawsuit From Former Contributor

BethesdaFan gameThe Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion RemasteredThe Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

Since 2012, a team of Elder Scrolls fans have been assembling a total conversion of Oblivion to run off the engine of its descendant, Skyrim. Known as “Skyblivion” the fan-project has spent over a decade in development. While a lengthy development is often filled with ups and downs, its latest woe is a rather unique one, as developers say that one of their former members is threatening litigation.

“Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivionâs development departed the project,” posted The Elder Scrolls Renewal Project. “We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure.”

A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG

— Skyblivion (@TESRSkyblivion) October 30, 2026

According to the statement, an unnamed volunteer contributor left the team a short time ago. Since leaving, there has been a great deal of contention around the work they left behind. The former developer, according to the post, objected to the “decompilation of parts of their work,” something bound to happen as other aspects are reworked and improved. In response, the disgruntled party sent a legal threat, demanding the real names of others involved.

To temper the situation, the statement says they decided to remove the code and contributions in question, but despite that the former member has “continued to intensify their threats.” In a video plea, Kyle Rebel says that one anonymous community member demanding the legal names of the others is unacceptable. In kind, they also ask supporters not to”make this a witch-hunt,” requesting pro-bono legal assistance and resources over any online campaign to sniff out the unnamed troll. The nature of their contributions, the reasons for their departure, and what contractual agreements were made (if any) are left unspecified.

“A “take your ball and go home” approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community that makes massive passion projects like this possible,” reads the statement. “While weâve consulted with legal counsel and are completely confident in our right to maintain the code they submitted, we had zero interest in holding onto friction or fighting a former team member.”

Skyblivion has become something of a Ship of Theseus. Originally aimed to be a direct port, work generally evolved into something closer to a hide-to-hair remake that would be implemented as a Steam mod. While anonymous, the team of hobby developers is estimated to have grown to around 40 strong. They had aimed for a 2025 release, though by the end of the year they admitted it would need more time. Obviously another hurdle was the release of Bethesdaâs own remastered Oblivion that same year, though the community said it wouldnât stop their efforts.

Fan-projects are no strangers to legal threats, many having to bow out or become entirely new when the official studios rattle their tail. In this case, however, Bethesda was vocally supportive of Skyblivion, and the litigation has come from within.

"We are putting in serious consideration on the sense of tempo."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"This time we are putting in serious consideration on the sense of tempo, back at Dawntrail we were being really careful in depicting new lands, new cultures, new encounters and this greatly slowed down the pacing on story progression. The fact that this did not align with the player's motivation of 'keep moving forward' shows shortcomings on my part as the director.

"For Evercold, segments that focus on above-mentioned elements are moved to side quests, and we made it so that players can enjoy them at their own pace after, and pay our attention to the sense of tempo," via the r/FFXIV subreddit.

As PC Gamer's premier 'I think too much about the story Dawntrail could've been' person (which is a proper, official title, don't look it up), I have some thoughts about this.

Now to be clear, this is a translated quote from a group interview, and while Yoshi-P is certainly involved in the process of writing any expansion, he's a game director, so he's got an overarching view rather than a handle on the nitty-gritty of a given storyline. However, I don't think the issue in Dawntrail was its over-emphasis on worldbuilding, it was a lack of interest in how that worldbuilding connected to character.

Sure, the whole 'talk to three people' questlines get deservedly dunked on as a clumsy vehicle for how this stuff gets conveyed, but I don't really have any problem with how Dawntrail sets up the continent of Tural itself. As a matter of fact, I think the baseline is all very interesting—a fledgling nation under a first king at the end of his life, forced to reckon with how succession will work? That's a fun setup.

The stumbling of Dawntrail is in how none of these worldbuilding details had knock-on effects for the characters in any real, meaningful way. We learn about these cultures, and they either barely come up again or they add little to the core emotional conflicts that the characters are going through, with the exception of the Mamool Ja and the Skydeep Cenote.

Gulool Ja Ja, the warrior-king soon to abdicate the throne, basically does no wrong throughout all the stories we learn of him (aside from his raising of Zoraal Ja, which isn't really explored anyway) giving absolutely nothing for the main cast to reflect on. Wuk Lamat's relationship with her siblings is never meaningfully or memorably explored in the context of the societies she's learning about.

Even the rite of succession messes up clean opportunities—there's a whole segment where contestants are randomly assigned to partners, and rather than use this as an opportunity to have Wuk Lamat, say, paired with someone she doesn't like, she just gets put with Koana and nothing really happens as a result.

Textured worldbuilding isn't the issue—the issue is that worldbuilding should generally feed back into the overarching themes and narrative. I'm not sure simply offloading all of it into the story's sidequests is the answer, rather than having a considered effort to make it interesting and relevant to the characters at hand.

But again, I'm not expecting Yoshi-P to sate my hunger for nitty-gritty nuance through the filter of translation in a group interview—and the current Evercold introductory patch story does give me hope, given there's already been some effective show-not-tell worldbuilding in it. The fact Visna freaks out about us approaching without stating our brand is great, it immediately sets the stakes for life in this ice-covered world without beating us over the head with it. So there is genuine hope that FF14's story really is returning to form.

#3792. EA reportedly closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between Mass Effect 5 and Star Wars Battlefront 3

And it chose the "less risky, more predictable bet".

A new report has revealed that EA closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between investing in one of two sci-fi projects: a new Mass Effect game or a new Star Wars Battlefront game. And it chose the latter.

The revelation comes from Bloomberg, which heard from "people familiar with the company's strategy" that the "recent emergence" of an opportunity to develop a third Battlefront game meant EA - a company saddled with $18bn in debt because of the recent leveraged buyout - would have two sci-fi projects, each likely to cost hundreds of millions of dollars to make.

It couldn't afford to make both of them so EA executives chose Star Wars Battlefront 3, because it was seen "as a less risky, more predictable bet than a new Mass Effect", Bloomberg reported - despite development for the game not even having begun yet.

An EA spokesperson said the company had "collectively reached this decision following months of planning, review, and analysis, including careful consideration of evolving business conditions, industry dynamics, and our long-term priorities". "While this is never easy," the spokesperson went on, "we ultimately have to make tough decisions to focus our teams on the biggest opportunities for our future, including investing in new projects across our portfolio."

The report highlights a few other contributing factors in EA's decision, including BioWare's unfavourable recent track record and a reorganisation of its executive ranks to include more EA Sports people, in favour of those advocating for BioWare. EA bosses even lamented Dragon Age: Veilguard's sales, suggesting it would have been better if the title was 'a live service game'.

Last week, following the announcement of BioWare's closure and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, an internal video for the project - known as Mass Effect Universe - was leaked, showing what appears to be a pre-rendered visualisation of it. The game was said to take place 600 years after the Reaper war, in the midst of a galactic cold war, and to have the player be "a cross between John Wick and James Bond" in terms of what they'd be capable of.

There was a promise of "Hitman-style freedom" in approaching levels, romance that "wasn't being sanitised", and for connections between the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies. It's not clear how much work was done on it, but clearly a lot of planning had been done - far more, certainly, than has been done on Battlefront 3.

EA's Star Wars Battlefront 2 was released in 2017 and struggled, initially, to convince - partly because it was riddled with loot boxes. But years of adjustments and improvements left it in a much better place.

#3789. Patrick Stewart, Our Captain Of Multimedia CD-ROM Edutainment

In 1997, Patrick Stewart took me on a voyage through the stars from the comfort of the family computer room. An interactive expansion of a 1993 video cassette, Nine Worlds allowed you to travel the solar system, pick up gift shop postcards, scientific and cultural history of each neighboring planet, all accompanied by bombastic (and slightly compressed) renditions of Gustav Holstâs famous celestial suites. And of course, with the guided audio tour from Stewart himself, whose impassioned chronology of Mars only netted me a C+ on my homework.

“To the Romans and Greeks, it was the god of war,” orates computer Stewart, “to others IT WAS THE RED EYE OF THE DEVIL HIMSELF!”

In the days since his shocking passing, fans have found themselves with so much to parse from the multifaceted thespian. Of course, to most, he was the eloquent, insightful Captain Jean-Luc Picard, whose fascinations of the cosmos led the crew on Star Trek: The Next Generation. To others he was the fatherly Professor X across the sprawling X-Men films. He was also a master of stagecraft, an outspoken advocate, a baker of erotic cakes, and a Beavis and Butt-Head superfan.

To those of a certain age, he was also an educator. Or, more specifically, an edutainer. Following Mystâs bank-making showcase of what CD-ROMs were capable of, classrooms and home computers experienced a surge of educational software. There had long existed Math Blasters and illustrious typing teachers, but with the assistance of compressed video and tinny audio, publishers sought to bring the classroom experience home.

While most celebrities needed to be charged on a DUI to edutain, the Next Gen crew seemed eager to moonlight as teachers. Of course, LeVar Burton had long hosted Reading Rainbow by the time he donned La Forgeâs visor, setting some precedent. While Riker was elsewhere teaching celebrity poker, Patrick Stewart captained numerous suites of multimedia CD-ROMs.

"Now go, explore, and enjoy. The adventure is yours."

— âï¸Beth âï¸ (@rollinrabbit.bsky.social) 2026-10-29T20:27:45.134Z

Sure, narrating a cultural history of our solar system makes sense given his resume, but Stewart was also recruited to guide young users in Compton’s Interactive Encyclopedia, a literary play-by-play of the Titanicâs final hours, among many other loose discs. His outstanding voice, powerful but kind, made him an ideal messenger for worldly information. It was an era where people were still learning how to use these machines, never mind learn from them. And in this brief era of scholarly CD, Stewart passed on the fascinations exhibited by his most famed performances.

While it didnât do me a ton of good on my immediate school work, many of these pieces of software imparted some deeply rooted pieces of information, continuing to rattle around my skull. As someone who would later on adore passing out to Carl Sagan, I didnât fully appreciate the psychic history of the Red Planet offered by Stewart. But the amount of context and culture squished into a meager disc is a fascination of its own. Where and how kids learn from computers going forward might be dubious, but there was an era of enthusiasm to reimagining games and education. When we aspired to reach higher, Stewart found himself a star there too.

#3788. Crimson Desert Enhanced Edition gets a surprise demo on PlayStation and Xbox, lets you play for 5 hours and carry over your save data

Crimson Desert is one of 2026's most successful releases. The game managed to sell over 6 million copies in just three months, and ended up being so profitable that its publisher ended up giving each employee at development studio Pearl Abyss a $3,400 bonus. Since launch, the dev has been committed to improving the game and correcting some of the more egregious issues that were present at launch.

Now, over half a year after its launch - and with the publisher's revenue up a massive 419 percent - it seems the company is eager to let anyone that hasn't yet purchased the game try it out, completely free. To celebrate the launch of the delayed Charting the Unknown DLC, which came out yesterday, Pearl Abyss has made the first five hours of the game completely free to play for (nearly) anyone on Xbox or PlayStation.

Any trial progress you make carries over to the full game if you decide to purchase it, and once your five hours are up, that's it - you can't restart the trial on a different save or something like that. The timer is final.

Charting the Unknown is the first bit of DLC for the game - there's likely more to come - and a Switch 2 version of the sandbox fantasy RPG is currently in development. #3787. How to collect map fragments in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

At every turn, Fortnite Treasure Hunters challenges you to embark on all kinds of tricky scavenger hunts. Just about every mission and every item you can find around the island involves some kind of treasure hunt, as is the case with the collect map fragments quest.

This is one of the most difficult tasks you’ll face, as it requires a lot of time, effort, and careful searching to get it done. It does grant a pretty special prize for completion, though, so here’s how to collect map fragments in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

To complete the collect map fragments quest in Fortnite, you need to carefully scour the island to find and collect six map fragments. This quest is a bit of a tough one to get done, as it’s an overarching goal for the entire mini-season rather than a task you can get done right away.

Each week, a new map fragment will be added to the island. Because of this, you cannot complete this mission all at once, and instead need to work on it over time as the season progresses.

Throughout the season, a fresh map fragment will arrive as each new section of the Adventure tab is unlocked. These fragments correspond to the arrival of additional special characters around the island, like Lil Uzi Vert, A$AP Rocky, and Cap’n Hatsune Miku.

Since you need to collect a total of six map fragments, this mission takes a full six weeks to get done. You can check the Adventure section under the Treasure tab on the home page to see which part of this quest is live.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Each of the six map fragments can only be found at one specific location around the Fortnite island. All of them are only available to collect after their initial unlock date has arrived, so you have to wait to collect them all.

Here’s when each map fragment unlocks and a breakdown of where to find each one. Some details have been revealed for map fragments ahead of their arrival, while others are entirely unknown. We’ll update all details here as they become available to help you obtain them all.

Fully finishing the collect map fragments quest unlocks the X Marks The Zero Point Sliver Loading Screen as a reward. This is a completely free reward that’s automatically granted once you’ve successfully gathered all six map fragments. You also get 10,000 XP for each piece you find.

While you wait for more map fragments to unlock, there are lots of other missions to keep you busy around the island. Some good ones to work on are using Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests, unlocking all Treasure Hunters battle pass skins, and solving the Frog Statue puzzle.

Valve's second mighty expensive, yet mighty impressive VR headset, the Steam Frame, launched in the latter half of September, meaning October was the first full month where players could actually use it. The latest Steam Hardware Survey suggests a rather big bump in usage for Valve's VR headset this past month.

In September, the Steam Frame accounted for just 0.41% of VR headset usage. In October, that number jumped to 4.13%. That means it surpassed the Oculus Rift S, Sony PS VR2, HTC Vive, Windows Mixed Reality (which is a platform, as opposed to a single headset), the first Oculus Rift and Bigscreen Beyond. It is now the sixth most popular VR headset, sitting just .37% behind the Pico 4, and a hefty 24.14% behind the Meta Quest 3.

The 3.72% increase for the Steam Frame is the biggest jump upwards in October, and the biggest tumble was taken by the Oculus Quest 2, which lost 3.57%.

The Steam Frame officially released on September 18, with preorders going live on September 14, but that doesn't mean buyers got their hands on the headset on the day it went live. So the bump can not only be partially attributed to continued sales over October, but also to shipping times.

It's also worth noting that both the 256 GB and 1 TB models are backordered, meaning even if you sign up for one now, you will simply be put on a waiting list. That means Frame usage is unlikely to entirely stagnate from here.

Given the Steam Frame has enjoyed such a large bump even with customers struggling to get their hands on the headset, this suggests the VR market on Steam isn't huge. Though it is worth taking these stats with a pinch of salt.

The Steam Hardware Survey is an opt-in survey Valve takes every month. This means it only looks at a fraction of Steam users to get general statistics. This is why stats tend to change a tad each month. For instance, the Nvidia GeForce RTX 3060 is currently the most popular graphics card in the survey, but it saw a 0.08% increase last month. The RTX 4060 saw a downward shift of 0.40%, pushing it below the RTX 3060.

As such, the Hardware Survey can only ever give a rough reading of usage each month, but it still seems like a good sign for Valve's latest bit of hardware.

#3784. Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3's online servers are temporarily going dark, FromSoftware announces

Things might get even darker over in the world of Lordran without those silly, only sometimes helpful notes left by other players. Developer FromSoftware has announced that it's temporarily closing Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 servers because of an unspecified issue.

"Due to a server issue, the game servers for the following titles will be temporarily unavailable on all platforms," the RPG studio tweeted earlier today, before naming Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3.

While the server shutdown won't last forever, FromSoftware hasn't told series fans when exactly they can expect online play to be restored. That presumably means PvP invasions, summon signs and in-game messages that try to troll you off a cliff are unavailable for the time being.

"We will provide updates once we have information regarding the server restoration time. We apologize for the inconvenience," the studio added. I hope you've stocked up on Estus Flasks, at least.

Of course, this isn't the first time the Dark Souls trilogy has had to contend with server problems. In 2022, Bandai Namco took servers for all three Dark Souls games offline due to a security vulnerability affecting Dark Souls 3. The threequel went dark once again a few months later.

FromSoftware's next game The Duskbloods - the one with the jetpacks and vampires and a cute bird thing - hasn't been any luckier, either. The multiplayer-focused game's first network test had to be taken offline early due to similarly vague "server issues". More recently, FromSoftware delayed its Switch 2 exclusive into next year.

"While development of The Duskbloods is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027," the developer tweeted this week. "We apologise to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support."

#3783. Easiest way to get the Pirate Token Shop in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

The Treasure Hunters mini-season has sent all Fortnite players on a wild hunt, as the Pirate Shop has several premium items for you to redeem at zero cost. Typically, you’ll need to spend V-Bucks to buy these items, but you can get all of this for free for a limited period of time. It depends on you accessing the Pirate Token Shop first.

To raise your chances, you will have to open as many regular chests as possible during your adventures. You can, however, accelerate the process with a few simple tricks.

To get the tokens, you have to open as many chests as possible. That’s the only way to obtain it. However, here’s how you can strategize the whole process.

First, you have to drop on the map and look in areas that have a higher concentration of these chests. If you visit a spot that has a limited number of chests, chances are that someone else might have opened them and received the rewards. More chests provide you with more opportunities to find the tokens.

Next, you’ll want to get the Plundarggh Sprite. This sprite increases your movement speed whenever you open a chest. This fits nicely into our loop since we will open as many chests as possible. Doing so will increase your speed, and this allows you to save time while traveling between different chests.

Finally, you’ll want to play in squad fill if you don’t have friends. All members of the party will get the access tokens if one of you gets it from the chest. Hence, playing in a party makes complete sense since you can open the number of chests three times in a round, which you might not be able to do alone.

Ultimately, it will boil down to your luck when it comes to unlocking the Pirate Shop. Once done, you’ll have 14 days to redeem all the available rewards and applicable cosmetics.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I'm buzzing through the Dungeon Crawler Carl series this year, and my 8-year-old daughter gets so jealous every time she sees it. She loves cats, dinosaurs, and adventure, so in her mind, there's no reason she shouldn't be able to read it as well or watch the upcoming series when it premieres for those with a Peacock subscription.

Of course, anyone who has read the books knows that they're hardly appropriate for a young audience. One would have to remove all the gore, swearing, and raunchy jokes for it to even begin to pass for most parents, which gave me an idea. What if Princess Donut was able to retell the events of DCC, but in the way she'd tell it to her dinosaur "child," Mongo?

I love the way Princess Donut treats and refers to Mongo like he's a child, despite the fact that he's a raptor regularly tearing their enemies to bits. She's always worried about him being traumatized, or "appalled," which got me thinking. It would be hilarious to read Donut recalling their past adventures to Mongo, and self-censoring the raunch along the way.

I just imagine my daughter laughing as I'd tell her about Princess Donut dancing in the club, zapping goblins with her laser vision, and going on side tangents about her hatred for Cocker Spaniels. It would still be the Donut we know from the books, but she's adjusting it all for the audience it's intended for.

I think it would be important to have that, rather than standard narration. Donut is a gem of a character, and I think introducing children to that early on would only encourage them to check out the novels in full when they're of age later in life.

I've often thought about Carl being the narrator in Dungeon Crawler Carl, and how much the story might change if it were anyone else narrating. The things they'd focus on, compared to him, and the things they'd notice well before he did. I'm of the opinion that Donut might have a more entertaining telling of it all, which is part of the reason she's just the best.

Matt Dinniman Can Thank Jeopardy! For Making Dungeon Crawler Carl's Success Feel Real For His Mom's Friends

All this to say, part of this plight is because I also want to see how much I'd enjoy Donut retelling the story, even if it were geared toward children. Plus, there are already spinoffs in the works, like the upcoming comic featuring Florin.

If I could get the ball rolling on making Princess Donut's Bedtime Stories For Mongo, I definitely would. I'm not the author, however, so Matt Dinniman, if you have time between making the rest of the series, perhaps consider this pitch to sell the fun of Dungeon Crawler Carl to the children?

In the meantime, I'll keep reading the stories, waiting for the new books and announcements related to the upcoming series. I have a feeling we're about to be overwhelmed with news about the franchise over the next year, but I promise I won't let it break me.

After more than two decades dominating the PC MMO battlefield, it sounds like Blizzard Entertainment's taking the idea of a World of Warcraft console port more seriously than ever.

World of Warcraft: Forever's beta seems to have been immensely popular with fans of the series. It's a brand new third version of the iconic multiplayer game that sits alongside WoW's Classic and Retail portions, and it's recaptured many a lapsed Warcraft sicko with tons of good changes, big and small - one of which is controller support for the first time ever.

Speaking to GamesRadar about the decision to keep World of Warcraft: Forever exclusive to PC players, despite now supporting gamepads, vice president and executive producer Holly Longdale hinted that the fantasy game might just make its way to even more devices and players over time.

"What you just described is really what we're after," she told the outlet. "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want. But the first leg of that journey is getting gamepads working really well with World of Warcraft, and we thought Forever was the perfect place to start."

Longdale reckons all gaming platforms might become "more ubiquitous" in the future, as well. She specifically named the Xbox Project Helix, which is said to be a PC-console hybrid device of some kind. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed the next-gen console can even play your PC games earlier in the year.

"Honestly, we just want to be able to play it anywhere. We've seen people getting it working on the ROG Ally X," Longdale added. "I think just doing some of the work we're doing on gamepad is going to give players a lot of flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles."

World of Warcraft: Forever properly launches on the 4th of November.

Elsewhere, Longdale acknowledged that some of the developer's decisions won't make everybody equally happy: "I think the lesson we learned the most over time is 'You don't listen to the loudest people in the room.'"

#3780. Best Roblox song IDs

There’s just something about listening to your favorite music in a public setting and forcing it upon the ears of others. Roblox has turned this real-world nuisance into a series of games on its platform.

Using a database of uploaded songs, players can input Song IDs to blast their song of choice directly into the ears of strangers all over the world. Here are some of the best.

Prior to a change in March 2022, users could upload virtually any audio file and have it be playable in any game that supported the boombox via a Song ID. The change retroactively made any audio longer than six seconds private. This meant that if you weren’t the person who had originally uploaded the audio file, you would no longer be able to play or hear the sound.

This means the vast majority of Song ID repositories are now functionally useless, and users have been restricted to a much smaller selection of songs and sound clips of varying quality. One important thing to know is that there’s no guarantee that any individual Song ID may work, as they can be made private by either Roblox staff or the user who uploaded it.

Below are 30 absolute bangers to entertain yourself and possibly others around you. I have personally confirmed that each is working at the time of this writing. Go forth, aspiring DJs!

To search for music codes on Roblox, follow these steps:

You’ll discover many sections on the Audio page, from the top Roblox Song IDs to the newest hits of the day. After you find a song, you can get its ID through ‘More Info.’ Discover the correct number from your URL. For instance, mine came out to ‘create.roblox.com/store/asset/75793628822368/Mirage-Portal.’ Thus, the bolded numbers would be utilized as the Song ID.

Playing music in Roblox varies in each game, as they all have different methods. Sometimes, it can cost money with Robux, while other times, it doesn’t cost a thing. To play music for free, play Catalog Heaven, a game that allows you to customize your avatar and battle nearby bases. Once you start playing, select ‘Catalog’ and type in Boombox. There will be a few choices here, including the Boombox Gear 3.0 and Golden Super Fly Boombox. Choose one of them to trigger a prompt to enter Roblox music codes.

Tap on the Boombox again if you want to change songs. You can also stop the music by unequipping it in your inventory. Besides Catalog Heaven, you can see if other games permit music. I discovered that Jailbreak features a Car Stereo mechanic, costing 200 Robux. With this title, you can type in ‘R’ or tap the radio on the bottom-right corner of the screen. Then, enter any Song ID you prefer to listen to some tunes on Jailbreak.

For the most part, it seems like Roblox titles that use music codes require a subscription pass. Therefore, if you’re unsure whether your game is compatible, check the title’s Subscription & Passes section to see if there’s a radio or stereo feature.

Only Roblox game developers can create custom music playlists. It’s associated with a tool used in scripting to create soundtracks for various worlds. If you’re a player, you must manually enter each ID to make your own version of a playlist.

"We bought a wonderful sample library from a piano in Chernobyl that someone had found in the Forbidden Zone. Someone went there and made a sample library from that old piano. So we bought that one and used it," via Arc Raiders' YouTube channel.

Arc Raiders has a terrific soundscape, although it can sometimes be hard to hear it when you're getting hunted down by your fellow players or bloodthirsty arcs. The game is quite quiet, aside from the occasional sound of distant gunfire, the clicks and cracks from small roaming arcs, and the noise of shuffling scrap as raiders sort through abandoned buildings for valuable items. But perhaps the best noise in all of Arc Raiders comes from the few instruments raiders can find amid the rubble.

"One of the gameplay designers, really early on, made a trumpet," Pajor says. "And it was so out of place, and we were like 'why are we making it?'" The musical items in Arc Raiders serve multiple purposes. There's the social incentive to play an instrument, to bond with strangers and just show them that you're a harmless, relatively chill dude. But there's also the strategic purpose of using noises to lure arcs. Perhaps you're herding them into a trap or ambush or maybe you're trying to distract the aggro of one arc away from another vulnerable player.

Avid players of Arc Raiders will notice, however, that there's no trumpet available in game. Well that's because the trumpet eventually became what we now know as the lure grenade. Apparently a playable trumpet was just too silly to the devs at first, so they settled on something a bit more useful. But now, over a year later from launch players can enjoy multiple instruments like the piano, guitar, harmonica, flute, banjo, recorder, and the trusty shaker.

"It's been almost seven years of exploring this world. [Composers Patrik Andrén and Johan Söderqvist] used to be performing musicians before they became composers so they have a lot of friends who are Sweden's best jazz musicians," Pajor adds. "So a lot of the sounds in the game are quite unique because they are making the sound libraries.

"It's their commitment to building a world; they're phenomenal world builders. So eager to understand what the game is and what the world is. They are also very demanding to work with, because they have so many ideas."

Aside from the Chernobyl piano, which is certainly one of the stranger sources of music I've heard of, composers Andrén and Söderqvist are also known for their abstract use of everyday items to make music and noises.

A lot of raw synthesisers are used to create arc-adjacent noises, but they've also hooked up different kinds of fruits to a synthesiser to grab some slightly weirder sounds. All in all, out of a three hour recording session there's usually only three minutes of usable sounds, "because it's sheer weirdness" but those three minutes "are really really really cool", Söderqvist adds, and stresses that you simply can't obtain these fantastically strange sounds another way.

#3777. GOTY hopeful Mina the Hollower bought the studio financial stability "for now," while the Shovel Knight devs work on a new 3D game

Yacht Club Games has confirmed that most of its developers are now working on a brand new 3D game (potentially Shovel Knight 3D), after the critically-acclaimed Mina the Hollower did well enough for the team to continue.

Before launching its old-school adventure game earlier this year, Yacht Club described Mina the Hollower as a "make-or-break" moment for the beloved indie studio. A global pandemic and a failed experiment to turn Yacht Club into a multi-project studio had left the developer on thin ice, it seems.

But Mina the Hollower sold well enough to buy the studio more time, according to a new Reddit AMA full of interesting tidbits. Asked if Mina was able to secure financial stability for the company, Sean Velasco simply said "yes… for now!" Mina managed to sell over 500,000 copies in its first two weeks, so it's well on its way to the one million copies the devs were once hoping for.

For the foreseeable future, the devs aren't ready to talk about the kinds of DLC and spin-offs and follow-ups that dear old Shovel Knight enjoyed for many years, but they're not abandoning their newest baby either. "We're working on more post-release features," the devs wrote, which includes "expanded randomizer options, enemy and boss randomization, more modifiers, speedrunner features" and more ways "to do even more in Mina."

Another fan also asked the folks at Yacht Club about their unannounced 3D Shovel Knight game - Velasco previously told Bloomberg that the game was halfway done before the entire studio put all hands on deck for Mina, and pivoted back into a one-game outfit. Alec Faulkner stopped short of confirming Shovel Knight 3D, but said "most of us are currently working on a 3D game, yes!" Alright then, Alec, keep your secrets. "Not sayin more! Other than that it’s gonna be soooooooo awesome."

Co-founder Nick Wozniac went further into the state of the developer, and why splitting the team in half was probably a mistake. Here's what he had to say on the matter: "Sales are the things that keep the company afloat so it's not born from greed (mostly) that we say we'd love to see more sales, it's all about continuing to work together and make great games and reaping the rewards along the way. We are doing ok and learned a lot this cycle. I think we learned mostly that keeping the team tight and focused is what helped Mina land. Splitting the team up to work on two games was something we could have corrected a long time ago but I'm glad to be where we are now. Just gotta pocket those lessons and use them to drive you forward."

Eurogamer's five-star Mina the Hollower review called it an "adventure that takes inspiration from the greats."
