#3776. A former volunteer is threatening legal action against fan-made game project Skyblivion

A former volunteer is threatening legal action against Skyblivion, the long-running fan remake of Oblivion built in Skyrim's engine, over code they contributed to the project.

The unofficial project, which remakes 2006's The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion, is being made by volunteers from the TES Renewal Project, the modding group that also works on Morrowind remake Skywind.

Bethesda has allowed the project to continue on condition that it replaces all of the original game's assets, and the team continued working on it after Bethesda released its own Oblivion Remastered in April 2025.

In a statement posted to Twitter/X on 30th October, the Skyblivion team said that after the volunteer left, the two sides disagreed over the "continued use and maintenance" of their work.

A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG

The main issue was the team's decompilation of parts of that code, which it said was needed "to maintain functionality and fix issues" after its access to the original source code repository was revoked.

According to the team, the volunteer then "escalated to sending legal threats", including demands for the real names and home addresses of its volunteer team leads. The team said this was "something we couldn't accept and think is disproportionate".

The team said it has consulted legal counsel and is "completely confident in our right to maintain the code they submitted". Even so, it said it removed the code "to protect our volunteers from undue stress and ensure a clean break", rebuilding that system from scratch.

Despite this, it says the threats have continued. Its post says the former volunteer is "attempting to sue", but it's not clear whether a lawsuit has actually been filed. The volunteer has not been named.

"Please don't make this a witch-hunt," the team told fans, adding that it wishes the former volunteer "the very best" and hopes to "get this resolved as soon as possible and get on with our planned release of Skyblivion".

Last December, the team delayed Skyblivion from 2025 into 2026.

#3775. Dave Bautista shows off Kratos physique after gaining 20 pounds of muscle for God of War TV series

From WWE to Guardian of the Galaxy to God of War, Dave Bautista is really flexing, both literally and figuratively.

It’s been just over two months since Dave Bautista was confirmed as the new Kratos in the Amazon Prime Video God of War series, replacing injured actor Ryan Hurst, but the man formerly known as WWE’s “The Animal” proudly displayed his god-like physique on Instagram yesterday.

Bautista says he’s now at 250 pounds, which is still quite a bit lighter than what he used to wrestle at in the WWE, when he routinely took to the ring at around 290. But after retiring from in-ring competition and focusing on acting, he’s since lost a lot of that weight and began putting it back on this summer.

Bautista was announced as Hurst’s replacement on Aug. 20, just a few months after the latter tore his pectoral muscle while filming and forcing Prime Video to scramble. Bautista was waiting in the wings, and he since got to work in the gym to be ready to get into the white and red paint and play father to a demigod.

It’s been fun to watch Bautista’s career, coming from his wrestling beginnings, to then taking on the role of Drax the Destroyer in the Marvel Cinematic Universe for several years of fun and iconic moments, and moving on to all sorts of varied acting roles since. This may be his biggest challenge yet, however, as he’s now 57 years old and this is quite a physically demanding role, as evidenced by Hurst’s on-set injury that helped land him the job.

Outside of Bautista, the God of War show’s cast is stacked, boasting a pantheon of Norse mythology along with talented actors: Callum Vinson as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, Ed Skrein as Baldur, Max Parker as Heimdall, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor, Teresa Palmer as Sif, Alastair Duncan as Mimir, Jeff Gulka as Sindri, Danny Woodburn as Brok, and more.

Dave Bautista reveals he has gained 20 more pounds of muscle for playing Kratos in ‘GOD OF WAR’.He has now reached 250 pounds. pic.twitter.com/fUOr0P7EAB

There’s currently no premiere date set for God of War on Prime Video, but it’s likely at least a year away, as Bautista now begins shooting and reshooting scenes that already took place early this summer with Hurst.

Potentially getting much more out of existing hardware is nothing to sniff at.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While I go 'oo' at every perfectly lit videogame vista, ray tracing can sometimes make my gaming rig go 'HNNNG'. I love a traced ray as much as the next person, but realistic reflections and lighting can be a bit of a memory hog. Thankfully, Microsoft is previewing something new for DirectX that could significantly take the load off many ageing rigs.

It's a pair of features called 'Clustered Geometry' and 'Partitioned TLAS'. At the risk of oversimplifying, you can think of this DirectX update as bringing tech very similar to Nvidia RTX Mega Geometry to every other GPU vendor.

Obviously there's more to it than that, though, with Microsoft describing this as the "most significant update [to DXR] since its debut in 2018." Top line: Microsoft's own testing of this update suggests it could reduce ray tracing memory load by as much as 90% without the need for a team green GPU (via Techspot).

So, how does it work? Well, without this update, ray tracing is already beaming between less detailed versions of the geometry you see in-game. Traditional ray tracing tech does this because bouncing around detailed models afresh for every frame would simply take too long.

Clustered geometry slices up the detailed models into neat little packages of 256 triangles or fewer. Partitioned TLAS then does a similar thing for the entire videogame vista, splitting a scene into smaller regions. Why? Well, rather than searching the entire map every time, looking for what's changed and updating the frame accordingly, the ol' dread pirate Ray Tracing needs only to run their finger over the quadrants they know are different, marking the spot with 'X'—or something like that, the metaphor got away from me a bit in the middle there.

Basically, this fresh DirectX tech massively simplifies the ray tracing data your rig has to check and update frame to frame. That could free up a whole lotta memory, with Microsoft demonstrating a reduction of 7.5 GB to 774 MB on an AMD Radeon RX 9070. Obviously, frame rates also benefitted, jumping from a wince-worthy 1.2 fps to a very impressive 79 fps in Microsoft's testing.

Now, this isn't really a case of simply installing an update and, 'whee, you're flying!' Microsoft issues a fair few caveats—for one thing, not all games are going to replicate the wins its specialised test environment saw.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

For another, working with clustered geometry and all of those packages of up to 256 triangles uses a lot more temporary scratch memory compared to traditional tech—that presents its own logistical concerns for game developers.

It's also worth reiterating that this update is not yet widely available, and there's no word yet on when PC gamers like you and me will be able to get our mitts on it either. If you feel like going sicko mode, though, Microsoft writes you can gain access to experimental features like this by using "matching Agility SDK preview headers and runtime, a supporting driver, and Windows Developer Mode."

Still, the potential to cut down memory usage without needing to buy any new hardware is very promising during these times of runaway pricing for both memory and GPUs. If I can put off a pricey upgrade for a few years more, I'll be happy.

#3773. Google’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Egg Makes The Search Engine What It Always Should’ve Been

GoogleThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Google’s cashing in on the nostalgia reawakened by the Ocarina of Time remake. If you type “zelda” into the Google search bar, you’ll get a glowing, hovering Master Sword in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. Click it, and the browser transports you and the search engine back in time to 1998, when everything was good and nothing hurt, or at least when it wasn’t an absolute pain in the ass to try to find something via Google.

The Google page is bedecked in its old livery: the bygone logo with the exclamation mark, along with old blue links in Times New Roman-ish font and listed, blessedly, in order of importance and relevance. No AI search results, no pesky shopping links, no ads. It’s a big ol’ beacon reminding you of a time when the web held the promise of unlimited information at your fingertips, and wasn’t yet the enshittified, barely ethical infomercial it has become. All for a little “Zelda” joke.

It’s not just “zelda” that’ll get you the nostalgia easter egg. “Ocarina of Time” will get you there too. It’s actually quite funny that Google’s reminding us now of the time when it didn’t suck. Last week, Google lost $475 billion in stock market value, the company’s worst-performing day on the stock market ever, with analysts noting that it had missed its ad revenue targets. The reason: Its own AI search product was eating into that ad revenue. Maybe Google should make the Zelda easter egg last a little longer.

How are Sydney Sweeney's bra and panties selling?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sydney Sweeney has gone into business in a big way, thanks to her lingerie brand, SYRN, and she's been making a lot of headlines because of it. Right off the bat, a wild bra stunt on the Hollywood sign proved controversial. However, the first line sold out in a matter of hours, So, how’s it really doing? In a new twist, a report claims the haters aren’t actually prevailing over SYRN.

Over the years, Sweeney has been the center of a ton of backlash for business-related moves. That includes selling her “bathwater” as soap, taking part in the viral “good jeans” campaign for American Eagle ad and most recently, for wearing nothing but footballs for her viral campaign with Novig. We can’t speak to how those ads are driving sales, but allegedly her work on her lingerie brand is really paying off.

This news comes months after reports of SYRN supposedly becoming a "disaster" after its launch, that said her "saleability is waning rapidly". But, a new report from Page Six, says something different. SYRN’s third quarter sales were reportedly double of the previous one. If this info is to be believed, the lingerie brand’s huge uptick in sales seems to be thanks to Sydney Sweeney’s Birthday Boobs collection, which launched on September 1. The big seller was her Blue Ditsy bra and panty set, which initially sold out on the first day it was launched.

Apparently, the ad for the bra and panty set was viewed by over 40 million people on Instagram alone! On paper, that's quite a marketing feat. Also, Sweeney’s Birthday Boobs collection, which is currently back on the website, reportedly generated over $2 million in sales.

While speaking about her brand, Sweeney previously said she made SYRN with the idea that everyone’s bodies are “different”, and should be served accordingly as far as lingerie goes. Sweeney’s campaigns, including those form SYRN, have received hate for catering to the “male gaze” over women, but the numbers suggest the ads seem to be leading to sales.

The A-lister herself has consistently propped up her brand, with social media serving as a prime forum for her to do so. From using socials to model her lingerie and to show off a SYRN-themed saloon, Sweeney hasn't held back with these marketing plugs. Check out one of her past posts from her Instagram stories below:

I also looked on a Reddit thread revolving around the quality of SYRN itself, and there seem to be quite a few positive comments on the pieces themselves. One person says they find them to be “the most flattering, prettiest, and best fitting” even against higher end brand pieces they own. Another person says the brand’s lace is “soft” and has “lasted in the wash”. Not everyone is satisfied, though, as one user says the “fit is awkward” and “scratchy and thin”.

SYRN is allegedly on track to have had an increase of 20 percent from October sales. That trend could continue to go upward considering Sweeney just launched her holiday shop with a viral ad where she channels Home Alone’s Kevin McAllister. And, ahead of that, her company dropped an ad that showed her channeling Cindy Lou Who. The new collection hasn’t quite done the Instagram viewing stats of her best-selling collection, but it certainly features a ton of seductive pieces, both on the lingerie front and for those looking for more cozy vibes, such as cable knit sweater sets, as holiday gifts.

With these recent updates in mind, Sydney Sweeney’s marketing style is apparently working. It'll be intriguing to see if SYRN continues to thrive into next year and become a beloved lingerie brand or not.

#3771. All Vault locations in Fortnite Treasure Hunters and how to get keys

Although treasures are a common sight while exploring the new One Piece-themed areas in Fortnite Treasure Hunters, vaults are still the best places to find those sought-after Pirate Shop Activation tokens and Legendary Sprites.

But don’t worry, you won’t need a master navigator or a Devil Fruit to find any of them. Here are all vault locations in Fortnite Treasure Hunters and how to get the keys needed to open them.

You can find a total of nine vaults scattered across the new Fortnite Treasure Hunters map, with most of its main regions housing one. The exceptions? Arlong Park, The Chest, and Plunder Port. In all areas but The $.$ Rocky, the vaults will be hidden behind a breakable sheet wall and located by a red flag.

The vaults can be opened by using universal Vault Keys and will house both a series of rare Treasure Chests and a guaranteed Sprite Chest. So prioritize them when looking to complete all steps in the Treasure Hunt Quest.

Among the locations above, reaching the Loot Laggon vault will require entering its secret area within the waterfall, while the one at Loguetown can only be found by heading to the city’s underground aqueduct.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Fortnite players can get Vault Keys as a rare loot by opening chests across the island or by eliminating players carrying them. When looking for one, we recommend focusing your search on either Busy Bay or Rubber Resort via their high number of guaranteed chest spawns per drop.

Certain sprites can also drop keys after leveling up, as well as boost your chances of finding them from regular chests. To learn more, check out all Sprites and abilities in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

While in possession of a key, the locations of the closest locked vaults will be marked on your map. As many will also be heading towards them, I recommend prioritizing the vault at Loot Laggon. After all, its natural camouflage might make most players pass it by and lower the chances that you might have to fight for the loot after unlocking it.

#3770. Silent Hill: Townfall adds new Hard difficulty in latest update

Silent Hill: Townfall has added a new Hard difficulty mode and rebalanced every existing setting to make room for it.

The update, patch 1.6.0, went live on PS5, Steam, and the Epic Games Store earlier this week, according to patch notes published by Konami. Konami said the rebalance is designed to create "a smoother difficulty curve for players to choose from".

As part of that rebalance, resources have been adjusted in some sections of the game, and enemies' hearing now gets sharper as the difficulty level goes up. Your position is now visible on the map in whichever mode you pick, while the reduction to the main enemy's attack severity now applies only in Story Mode.

Anyone who picks Nightmare for their first playthrough will now see a warning screen. The difficulty selection menu also gives a clearer summary of how the options differ.

SILENT HILL: TownfallNotice: Game Update (Patch 1.6.0)An update tuning gameplay and addressing some in-game issues is now available.Please check that the version number in the lower right corner of the main menu is displayed as v1.6.155963.*The PlayStation®5 version is…

The update also improves the valve status lighting for colourblind players, adds more hints and tutorials, and tweaks the wording of some puzzle hints and items. The options menu has been reorganised into clearer categories, and the controls remapping option has been renamed to make it clear that keyboard and mouse commands can be remapped there too, not just controllers.

PC players also get a new DLSS Ray Reconstruction option, alongside the usual general improvements and bug fixes.

To check you're on the latest version, look for v1.6.155963 in the lower right corner of the main menu on PC, or v1.6.156035 on PS5.

Developed by Screen Burn and published by Konami, Silent Hill: Townfall launched on PS5 and PC on 24th September. Matt said Townfall showed Silent Hill's "stellar revival continues as new developer Screen Burn melds stealth, meticulous world design, and a dash of social realism for a different sort of survival horror", and awarded it four out of five stars in Eurogamer's Silent Hill: Townfall review.

Meghan Markle was recently up for a big honor, thanks to one of her productions at Netflix. The Duchess of Sussex’s show, With Love, Meghan, was nominated for Outstanding Lifestyle Program at the 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards. The (non-televised) show took place this past Friday, October 30 in Los Angeles and, ultimately, Markle’s show didn’t win the award. Said honor was obtained by the dog-centric docuseries A Different Breed. Now, the Internet is sharing the same take on Markle’s series losing to one all about dogs.

With Love, Meghan – of which there are two seasons for Netflix subscription holders – sees Markle participation in beauty and home-based activities alongside special guests. Meanwhile, A Different Breed centers on dogs and their handlers as they compete in different athletic competitions. Upon learning that Markle’s show didn’t earn the gold trophy to Breed, a number of people took to X to share the same take about Markle losing the award to dogs. Check out just a few of the comments shared:

The loss itself isn’t the only topic of discussion that’s been circulating in regard to Markle’s nomination. Some commenters are also bringing up the Duchess’ absence from the awards show. As of this writing, an official reason for Markle – who recently moved back to the UK with her husband, Prince Harry, and their two kids – has not been given. Regardless, some users seem upset about Markle not showing up for the event.

Are Prince Harry And Meghan Markle Already Going To Return To The US Soon? The Latest

With Love, Meghan made headlines even before its debut in March 2025, as the show’s release was deemed “tone deaf” by some pundits due to its release coinciding with the LA wildfires. Many have chastised the show for a few key details, including the presence of Le Creuset cookware, which was considered too fancy for the average kitchen. When asked about that during an event, Markle reportedly lifted her hands and asked, “This is a thing, in 2025?

I honestly never thought I’d be in the position to write about a Meghan Markle-fronted production losing to a show about dogs. But, of course, the last thing I’d ever want to do is diminish the efforts of A Different Breed’s producers. So, on that note, congratulations to that creative team for the win, and kudos to Markle and co. for getting nominated. Also, those who want to check out the canine-centered series can stream it with a Prime Video subscription.

#3768. Final Fantasy 14 reveals Evercold’s second new job and February release date, with pre-orders opening next week

Plus Square Enix confirms Final Fantasy 14 has passed 35m registered accounts.

Final Fantasy 14's next expansion, Evercold, will launch on 23rd February 2027, and its second new job is zephyr, a physical ranged DPS that fights with a crossbow and a bird.

Producer and director Naoki Yoshida revealed the job during the opening keynote of the Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo. Zephyr pairs crossbow shots with support from an avian familiar called Nephele, and joins Bastion, the greatshield-wielding tank revealed as Evercold's first new job at Fan Festival Berlin earlier this year.

Pre-orders for Evercold and the previously announced Collector's Box open on Wednesday 4th November at 9am GMT. Anyone who pre-orders gets early access, plus a Wind-Up Köttr minion and Halone's Earring, which boosts EXP from defeating enemies by 30 percent. The in-game items are delivered as soon as you pre-order, so you can use the earring to level jobs before Evercold arrives.

The Collector's Box is physical goods only. It doesn't include the game, in-game items or pre-order bonuses. Inside you'll find an art box featuring an Evercold illustration by Yoshitaka Amano, a figure of the Warrior of Light as a reaper, an Ethos metal keychain, a Köttr mini plush, and a Tapestry of the Fourth.

The Square Enix Store is also selling a limited Collector's Bundle that pairs the box with a code for the Digital Collector's Edition on Windows or Mac. Players on PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, and Steam can buy the box on its own and pre-order the Digital Collector's Edition separately. The digital edition adds a Valhallar Odin mount, an Entreat Crystal emote, and a Crystal Skyltborg weapon for Bastion.

Square Enix also used the keynote to reveal a new Fierce raid difficulty, sitting between Normal and Savage; a new trailer for the Evangelion: Ghosts of Desire alliance raid crossover, plus tougher eight-player battles built around some of its bosses; and new Tetsuya Nomura artwork for Beyond the Lifestream, a raid series crossover with the Final Fantasy 7 Remake series.

We can also expect Evolved Combat Mode, which Square Enix says highlights each job's unique identity; Seasons, a new system that changes how item rewards are earned; and expanded character creation with new Character Action Skins. Expanded housing features, PvP updates, and a revamped companion chocobo system will follow from patch 8.1.

Final Fantasy 14 has passed 35 million registered accounts.

You can watch the full keynote on Twitch, and there's more on the official Evercold site.

Final Fantasy 14 is now available on Switch 2. The port was announced at the end of June.

#3767. Nearly 50 percent of all of last month’s Steam releases admit to containing AI slop

It seems like AI-generated content in video games isn’t going anywhere any time soon. In fact, it’s only getting worse.

A Redditor named ploz dug deep into the stats to find that 49.9 percent of all new games released in October 2026 disclosed that they were made with AI-generated content, which is a big increase from 26.4 percent one year ago. The scary part? The chart below begins in January 2024 (when Steam added AI disclosure options), when it was just 1.7 percent.

But the details don’t end there, as ploz revealed that 40.1 percent of all games released in 2026 so far use the AI-generated content tag. And in actuality, the number is likely way higher as there are sure to be devs that don’t disclose their AI usage in the listings, plus the AI disclosure only counts content you see or hear, and not anything used in coding.

The Redditor said it’s “mostly small games” that use the AI tag, saying that “47 percent of games with fewer than 10 reviews disclose AI, compared to 14 percent of games with 1,000+ reviews.” That’s not all that surprising, considering a lot of the AI-centric titles are made by smaller devs or those trying to quickly make a few bucks, but the reality is likely much different.

It feels like using AI to code is certainly not going anywhere, and I can’t really imagine how many devs are utilizing this to make their games, although I’d venture a guess to say it’s more than we even realize or could think of, considering it doesn’t need to be disclosed. Where it feels especially egregious is when it can be seen or heard or felt through things like dialogue, music, or in-game imagery.

For now, though, Steam does not offer a way to filter out games with AI-generated content from the store entirely, and as evidenced by this most recent Steam Next Fest, many players are annoyed with how outwardly obvious some of the games are becoming with their “AI slop.” Valve recently said it was “aware” of the complaints, but there’s no real timetable for a solution either.

The Punished, coming soon to the outstanding deckbuilder, draw their power from self-flagellation.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Their aesthetic? Chains, whips; spiked. Their mood? Afflicted, condemned, ritualistic. Their angels? Dark. Their maiden? Iron.

Friendship ended with dwarven gearsmiths; my new favorite clan in Monster Train 2 is the tortured edgelords.

The final faction being added to Monster Train 2, The Punished, arrive November 10 as a paid DLC. Their theme is self-damage, with new keywords and spells that, primarily, reward power in exchange for hurting yourself. Your pain? Enemies' bane.

Though existing MT2 clans like the Melting Remnant revolve around forms of sacrifice, The Punished are absolutely thirsty for it. They bring new keywords like Chained (enemy units take half the damage that your units take) that make damage an active solution to enemy waves. The self-flagellation angle likewise brings new purpose to some existing spells and equipment, and jives great with partner clans that provide protection from pain (Lazarus League) or more ways to inflict it (Pyreborne).

Damaging my own guys sounds like a risk-reward tactic that requires sophisticated play. In my first run as The Punished, I anticipated having to do brain-wracking calculus about how much damage to absorb. But instead, I've found the new clan to be one of the most powerful and, at least with one of their champions, easy to play.

A lot of that is down to the utility of their new gimmick, a big purple gem called the Monolith. Here's a breakdown of what makes it special:

"Level up the Monolith by sacrificing cards to earn Devotion, which grants Zeal, which buffs attack and HP for all units" kind of sounds like a line from a ProZD deckbuilder parody video (I will take any opportunity to reference the legendary Dairy Cow combo), but it's really not complicated. Click the purple crystal, make cards go away, permascale a little bit.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Though it can change the calculus for a few units, Zeal isn't that game-breaking on its own: usually you're just increasing the ceiling of a unit's HP to set up cards like Zealot's Halo, an equipment that gives +1 attack for every 1 HP you're missing.

More potent is The Punished's starter champion, Archus, an S-tier champ that amps damage based on lost HP, but has the versatility to debuff enemy damage as well. All of his build paths grant him Flight. His best variant deploys a "Darkshard" into the lane he flies into, a 0-attack artifact that does one of the following, on your choice:

Bloodshed is really, really powerful with the right unit pairings and a cheap spell or two that hurts yourself. What's wild is that Archus can deploy a Darkshard in every lane, with a cooldown of 2 on his flight ability. I might anticipate a nerf on that. Scaling your whole floor from received hits (including self-targeted spells!) is a wonderful way to accelerate sweepers or backline bruisers. Archus good.

Zariel, the other champ, is more advanced. The first angel cast out of heaven, "Zariel has been imprisoned for so long that her original crime has been forgotten to time." Sick. Although, you'd think that that would enable some kind of clemency?

Since her arms and wings are bound in chains, Zariel has no base attack. What she does have are three diverse paths that all play off sponging up as much damage as possible:

I asked Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke what combos the studio has found useful with Zariel. "A lot of Hellhorned cards like Branding Rite, Dark Deal, and Inferno work really well with Zariel's Pain and Chain paths. Pox is a great spell for consistent friendly damage, because it applies Decay 10 to all units," says Cooke. "Zariel's Pain Maiden path especially synergizes well with The Condemned, because the unit has Tenacious, it won't die to any friendly damage and it even amplifies the damage it takes and redirects it to an enemy, so it's great for pinging and stacking Pain while still killing enemies."

On my second run with Zariel, in the final rounds of a battle, I was dealing 1000 damage from her Paintouch ability, and I was doing it each turn because the ability has a cooldown of 1. On a couple other attempts, I couldn't create damage outputting units to pair with her quickly enough, and my run collapsed.

The superstar of the roster might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner.

This is one of the few weaknesses of The Punished—although several units have good base attack, instantaneous damage can be hard to acquire. Reaper of Suffering, The Punished's only sweeper, starts with a generous 60 attack (as much as Demon Fiend, a 4-cost Hellhorned unit), but it also starts Suppressed (meaning she cannot attack), needing a cooldown of 4 to expire before she emerges from that state. Taking damage decreases that cooldown, and incredibly, she heals to full HP when she emerges from Supressed and gains flight when you cross that threshold.

This isn't the only star unit on The Punished. Forsaken Berserker gains one multistrike for every two Monolith levels. Scarred Justicar, an uncommon, ended up being my damage solution on several runs. He simply gains +15 attack when hit by a friendly spell or ability, and considering one of the starter cards deals a gentle 2 damage, you can gain perhaps +30 or +45 attack in a round between spells and other effects. Slap a stack of multistrike and the new 3-cost equipment Sineater on him (Deal 8 damage to self, attack immediately, cooldown 2), and you have a high damage solution that just takes a little time to set up.

The superstar of the roster, though, might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner if you're able to draft it early. This stoic statue unit cannot be healed, but it gains +1 HP on revenge, astoundingly rare health permascaling that is set-and-forget simple. I found myself taking the "enemies gain multistrike" trial just to welcome more attacks against Penitent Sentinel. In some runs I was ending with nearly 300 HP, linked to a Titanite upgrade that effectively doubled that. Wild.

After 12 wins with The Punished, I love that they have several viable units to pick from, and how much they synergize with a variety of clans. I kept finding new ways of winning with Zariel, and my strangest victory was with this configuration:

I had no plan and was mostly freestyling through this, my upgrade selections weren't particularly strong. I was surprised to beat Savagery, let alone the Titans.

After 500 hours in Monster Train 2, it's refreshing to beat the game in an unexpected way. I truly thought this run was doomed because I had little traditional damage, no sweep, no tank, and no decapitating spells.

The Punished's masochistic theme works. And Shiny Shoe's treatment of these tortured angels is nice (their Carolina Panthers-blue skin helps them stand out, even among the pale blue Melting Remnant), though their stoic reverence doesn't leave a lot of room for quirk.

I would've loved to have seen a silly torture sicko among the roster, but I'll settle for Lasher, the first backline unit that hits any friendly units positioned in front of him for 1 damage (I don't recommend relying on Damage Shield when he's on the floor). Just think of it as giving your guys a helpful, spiked-chain pat on the back.

It's appropriate for the final update to a game I like a lot to hurt a little. But Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke did indicate that the studio may not be done with the franchise. "At this time The Punished is the last DLC planned for MT2," Cooke told me. "However, we love the world of Monster Train, and hope to work on more Monster Train games in the future!"

#3764. Activision to remove Itaewon crowd crush footage from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and apologises to victims' families

"We bow our heads in deep sympathy and apology to the bereaved families and victims."

Activision has apologised to the bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it will remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

In a new statement reported by Inven Global, Activision said the footage "will be completely removed" via a game update scheduled to roll out on 12th November.

The statement was issued in Korean, and the quotes come via Inven Global's AI-assisted, editor-reviewed translation.

As we reported earlier this week, the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died. The bereaved families' association and the Citizens Countermeasure Meeting called for its removal.

"We bow our heads in deep sympathy and apology to the bereaved families and victims who were deeply hurt by this incident, as well as to everyone we have caused concern," Activision said.

The publisher also said that Modern Warfare 4 "is a work of fiction created to provide realistic immersion", and it "never intended to evoke or trivialise any tragic event, including the Itaewon crowd crush" by using real news broadcast footage.

The controversy has also reached the South Korean government. During a press briefing, minister of the interior and safety Yun Ho-jung described the footage's inclusion as "secondary harm", and said: "I believe appropriate sanctions should be imposed".

"Using such a tragedy as material for a game, a form of entertainment or business, is something that should be refrained from as a matter of human ethics," Yun added. He said it was up to the relevant agencies to decide "whether to impose punishment or block it to make general access difficult".

Activision's earlier statement to Eurogamer said the opening cinematic "utilises some real world news coverage to establish the game's fictional narrative", and was "not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form".

#3763. Call of Duty: Warzone’s yearly refresh includes DMZ map Hajin in BR, MW4 guns, and reworks galore

Call of Duty’s Warzone is once again getting refreshed, this time to coincide with season one of Modern Warfare 4 this week.

Starting on Nov. 6, the new Hajin map from DMZ and MW4’s campaign will make its way to Warzone as a new battle royale experience, becoming the seventh different large-scale map to play home to the last-player-standing mode since the game launched in 2020.

The same locations found within Hajin in DMZ are on display here, bringing forth a new Gulag location and even the Korean-themed locale’s dynamic weather. The map will also include MW4’s weapons and mechanics, such as the ability to drag downed allies, and the new game’s weapons will now be the main loot pool for BR and Resurgence. Needless to say, those who’ve been playing MW4 since launch will be at an advantage out of the gate when it comes to crafting loadouts.

All weapons from Modern Warfare 2 (2022) through Black Ops 7 (2025) will be usable in Warzone, but they cannot be edited in the Gunsmith, so they are basically defunct. But many cosmetics like operators, operator skins, finishing moves, emblems, etc. will still be available in Warzone for season one of MW4.

New MW4 gameplay features in Warzone include a Zipline Launcher field upgrade to reach new heights, a rebalancing of Perks to equip into your loadouts, and a slew of new equipment like all of MW4’s killstreaks and more. And this is all in addition to new content coming for MW4 multiplayer and DMZ as well.

As for the respawn-enabled Resurgence, the new map Zodiac will also become the main attraction after appearing earlier this year as part of MW4’s beta. But if you’re in the mood for some classics, then you’re in luck, because both Verdansk and Rebirth Island will return to Warzone at some point mid-season for BR and Resurgence, respectively.

For more on MW4 Warzone in season one, check out the full post on the CoD blog.

#3762. Yakuza Spiritual Successor Gang Of Dragon Seemingly Cancelled As Nagoshi Studio Is Closed

Gang of DragonToshihiro NagoshiYakuza: Like a Dragon

Toshihiro Nagoshi, the former general director of Like a Dragon maker Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio, formed Nagoshi Studio with some colleagues from his time at Sega a few years ago, and the studio’s first big game was going to be Gang of Dragon, a Yakuza spiritual successor that was first revealed at the 2025 Game Awards. However, after months of speculation surrounding the studio’s fate, an announcement in an official Japanese government gazette has revealed that Nagoshi Studio is no more.

The November 2nd edition of the government gazette, which reports official business closures and openings among other things, reported the finalized closure of the studio and its operations as of October 31st. The studio had been supported by NetEase Games as part of the latter’s expansive investment into Japanese gaming. In recent months, however, the news surrounding NetEaseâs various investments into Japanese studios has been defined by closures and cuts to funding. We now know this includes Nagoshi Studio.

Rumors surrounding the future of the company had been circulating heavily in recent months. Earlier this year, it was reported that the company was facing a shortfall in cash as NetEase pulled funding, with the studio needing roughly $44.4 million in order to finish development on its cinematic action title. Since then, there have been numerous signs that the company was being forced to wind down operations and cancel the project after being unable to acquire the needed funds elsewhereâthe social media accounts for the studio have not been updated since February, with the YouTube channel deleted and website becoming inaccessible in May before being restored.

Zendaya, Timothée Chalamet and Florence Pugh have spent enough time promoting the Dune franchise together that you would think they have the group-photo routine down by now. Apparently, all it takes is one camera, one slightly cramped set, and Zendaya trying to maneuver everybody into position to throw that theory out the window. The entire Dune Part 3 cast reunited to celebrate Denis Villeneuve's first two Dune movies heading back to theaters, and the resulting video is wonderfully awkward.

In the video, posted by the official Dune movie Instagram account, Zendaya directly addresses a social media user's question about the first two installments possibly heading back to theaters. In the process, the actres nearly loses control of the whole operation, backs straight into Pugh and somehow leaves Chalamet looking like the guy who accidentally wandered into someone else's photo. Seriously, check out the post below, because you barely get a glimpse of the lead actor's eye, let alone his whole face:

The clip -- which also features Robert Pattinson, Jason Momoa and Anya Taylor-Joy -- starts simply enough, with Zendaya trying to pull everyone together for the shot. Then she backs up, bumps into Pugh, and has to readjust while laughing through it all. Meanwhile, Chalamet is practically being edited out of his own franchise reunion. It's incredibly silly, especially given how serious these three usually look in the movies.

Of course, the timing makes sense, though. Dune and Dune: Part Two return to IMAX this month ahead of Dune: Part Three's release. IMAX has formally announced that fans can catch both movies as a double feature on November 13, followed by individual screenings from November 14 through November 18. That's already a pretty good excuse to spend nearly six hours back on Arrakis. So Warner Bros. is sweetening the deal considerably.

Every screening will include exclusive footage from Dune: Part Three, which hits the 2026 movie calendar on December 18. That makes the re-release considerably more interesting for fans who have already seen the first two movies. And, if that footage is just nearly as impressive as what's been screened thus far, fans will have more incentive to grab their tickets and sandworm popcorn buckets for the threequel.

Villeneuve's latest film is a book-to-screen adaptation of the second novel in Frank Herbert's series, Dune Messiah, and brings Chalamet, Zendaya, and Pugh back as Paul Atreides, Chani, and Princess Irulan. The cast also includes the aforementioned Momoa, Pattinson and Taylor-Joy along with Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem and franchise newcomer Robert Pattinson.

So Much For Zendaya Taking A Break After Dune 3

We've already gotten some tantalizing information about the movie, including Chalamet saying he approached playing Paul differently this time around. The actor previously explained that while filming his final Dune movie, he dug deeper into tiny details of Paul's world than in the previous installments.

There are also plenty of reasons to keep an eye on Chani and Irulan. Zendaya became much more central to the story in Dune: Part Two, while Pugh's Princess Irulan should have considerably more to do as the story moves into Messiah. The third entry is set to be the final movie in Denis Villeneuve's critically acclaimed sci-fi trilogy, so we can probably expect one heck of an ending. Let's hope the film concludes a lot less awkwardly than this Instagram video.

But, before we get to the finale, audiences get another chance to see the first two movies in IMAX, plus a preview of what's coming next. While we wait, you can also revisit the first two Dune movies at home with an HBO Max subscription.

#3760. PUBG live-action series in the works at Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct and star

PUBG is being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Krafton announced the adaptation on 30th October, adding that Glover's brother Stephen, his writing partner on Atlanta, will join the project as a writer and executive producer.

The series will also be executive produced by Michael Schaefer for Neon TV, Fam Udeorji for Gilga, and Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee for LV3H. LV3H is Krafton's entertainment arm, and it's involved in both developing and producing the show.

There's no word yet on a release window, plot, or who else will star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

Earlier this month, Krafton revealed it was ending development of PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction shooter spin-off announced nearly a year ago. The publisher’s other games include Subnautica and InZoi.

#3758. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Devs Tried Adding Even More Fast Travel Points, But That Sucked

The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out this week, and by all accounts we’ve heard so far, it seems like a pretty faithful remake, albeit with a lot of (necessary, in my opinion) technical and mechanical smoothing out from the original. I don’t envy the devs working on this one (which we now know to be Nintendo EPD): Ocarina of Time is a classic that everyone has really, really strong feelings about. Deciding what to change and what not to change must have been a huge headache.

Which is why I’m so, so glad that Eiji Aonuma backtracked on his own ridiculous idea to add a bunch of new fast-travel pointsÂ to this game.

This came up during an Ask the Developer interview published by Nintendo today. Now, the original Ocarina of Time already has some fast travel, in that Link can eventually learn ocarina songs that will warp him to each of five of the game’s major dungeons, plus the Temple of Time. And honestly, that’s quite enough to be getting on with, thanks. One of these songs is actually necessary to even access its associated dungeon in the first place, as you need child Link at the Desert Colossus, but he can’t get into Gerudo Valley without being adult Link and riding Epona.

But at one point in the remake’s development, longtime Zelda producer and franchise steward Eiji Aonuma thought this wasn’t enough. As Aonuma explains, he observed that a lot of players tried to move around the world faster in the original by spamming Link’s dodge roll, which led him to think there may need to be a faster way to get around the world.

I thought we needed to address this in this new version. So I asked the team to add warp points that didnât exist in the original game, giving players access to shortcuts. But when we actually tried playing the game with those warp points, we realized that we were missing out on the moments of discovery that came from stopping along the way and wondering, âWait, whatâs this?â Through this development process, we were reminded once again just how important those moments are to the very structure of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. So even though I was the one who proposed adding warp points, they just weren’t working for me in the end, so I got the team to take them all back out again. (Laughs)

Honestly, what a relief. He’s spot on, really. I played Ocarina of Time for the first time back in January, and while there were times when I was grateful to have a quick way to get from, say, Zora’s Domain all the way back to Castle Town without hoofing it through multiple loading zones I’ve seen a dozen times before, a lot of my favorite discoveries in this game came from being forced to hike around and trip over interesting things. There are all sorts of hidden bits in Hyruleâheart pieces, rupees, goofy little characters.

I also just don’t know where you’d even put more fast travel points. I guess I can imagine Aonuma wanting to add warp points to places like Kokiri Forest, Lon Lon Ranch, Zora’s Domain, and other major spots. But if you did that, then why would you ever need to even be in Hyrule Field? Ocarina of Time is not a massive game! It does not take that long to cross Hyrule Field, especially on Epona! It’s pretty easy to get to all those spots from the temple warps! Kids these days don’t want to go on long walks through grassy, Peahat-ridden plains anymore!

Mostly I just think it’s funny that Aonuma both proposed this idea and ultimately rejected it. Elsewhere in the interview, Aonuma talks about how the development of this remake involved handing off this old classic to individuals who had never played it until they were put on the project and letting them make their own decisions about how much to alter:

If the producers say, âThis is how it should be,â the team would naturally feel obligated to do it that way. So I basically let the developers make whatever changes they genuinely felt were necessary. I wanted the team to make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time their own, and to follow through on their own ideas about what the game should be. That said, I did deliver my fair share of lectures along the way. (Laughs) I took a step back to observe how the younger members of the development team would reimagine The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time using the insights and answers they had arrived at on their own.

The remake of Ocarina of Time is out later this week, on November 5, and a second part of this Ask the Developer interview is dropping tomorrow. You should read the entirety of it when you get the chance, as it’s pretty neat, though it’s left me desperately wanting to hear whatever “bright and upbeat” piece of music Kondo originally composed for Ganondorf’s theme way back in the ’90s.

Preorders are opening up for physical editions of Nightdive's Thief Remaster, and at the high end, the studio is offering an homage to Thief's iconic original PC big box packaging in that shape we all know and love, the trapezoid. The only problem? Nightdive and partner Clear River Games are only offering it for Switch/Switch 2 and PS5.

It doesn't really, at least not as much as war and death and politics or whatever. But Thief's original '90s big box edition came in a jaunty little trapezoidal box unlike anything else on the market. It remains a visually striking, highly sought-after collector's item. It's fun, it's memorable, and it's a piece of PC gaming history. I've had to settle for my version of Thief Gold that came in a plain Jane regular box as a reissue.

It's not super surprising that Night Dive and Clear River eschewed a PC version of this physical release⁠—that's fairly common these days, even in boutique indie special editions. I had a similar "we're so back, it's so over" reaction when I saw that indie RPG heater Dread Delusion's limited physical edition had skipped PC.

But the hurt feels new all over again when it's a PC gaming icon like Thief, and a PC gaming phenomenon like the big box. I would have dropped a fat hundo on a physical PC version of Thief Remastered in a heartbeat⁠—it's why I live in an apartment and not a house.

And studios still do come out with physical editions of their PC games: My Baldur's Gate 3 big box has pride of place in my office. All told, it's just a slight bummer and frustration trying to drag down one of my most anticipated games. I'm still going to play the hell out of it when it comes out on December 3, though.

I'm rooting for GOG's proposal to bring back the big box. The company seems to be considering a boutique service where you can purchase physical versions of the games in your library, which sounds pretty rad to me.

#3754. Dune: Awakening's free Blood and Ice expansion swaps sand for snow on 1st December

Funcom's survival MMO Dune: Awakening is heading north with a free expansion that trades the deserts of Arrakis for a frozen new map.

The expansion, called Blood and Ice, will release on 1st December. Funcom said it adds "around 35 hours of new progression", along with new vehicle modules, augments, and specialisation traits. It's coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox.

The new map, called the Polar Sink, turns the game's usual survival loop upside down. Instead of protecting yourself from extreme heat, you'll need to find ways to stay warm, upgrading your gear with resources found only in the Polar Sink.

The map is split into two biomes, the tundra and the ice cap. You'll start in the tundra, where wealthy water shipper families have built lavish strongholds, before trying to get into the heavily guarded ice cap. Once you're in, you can harvest ice to cool your base equipment and speed up production.

According to Funcom, the expansion "brings the focus back to ground-level survival, with traversal, temperature management, and combat all playing important roles in your progression". The studio also said future updates will add more reasons to go back to the region.

Blood and Ice also brings a new Events tab to the main menu. Shortly after the expansion launches, a new event called Water Crisis will follow the current one, The Scourge. Funcom says every event can be completed in both single-player and multiplayer, and that it plans to run them more often, each with new stories and free rewards.

Funcom has also launched a cosmetics store, which it says will help fund continued development and free updates. The store will start with a rotating selection of items, including looks taken from the Dune films to coincide with Dune: Part Three's release in cinemas this December. The plan is to eventually make the full catalogue available at all times.

Several of the community's most-requested features are also on the way. Offline single-player is due this month, and from January 2027 you'll be able to copy characters from multiplayer servers to single-player, and from single-player to select private or self-hosted servers on PC. Full cross-play will also arrive in January 2027.

"We're far from done," Funcom said, adding that it has "ambitious plans for the year ahead", including major free updates in 2027. The studio says more than a million new players have joined since the game launched on consoles, alongside a rebuilt endgame, three DLCs, and the conclusion of the game's first story arc, Book One.

Just a couple of weeks ago, Norwegian developer Funcom, creator of Dune: Awakening and Conan Exiles - and many other games - confirmed it was entering a period of restructuring and bracing for layoffs as a result. You may remember the company making a similar move this time last year, months after the initial PC release of Dune: Awakening.

Witney Carson just blew viewers away by competing on this season of Dancing with the Stars during her second trimester of pregnancy. Since she and her partner, Guillermo Rodriguez, were eliminated during Super Bowl night, Carson has been officially putting her focus on preparing for the arrival of her third baby. But that didn’t stop her from showing up for this year’s family Halloween costume. The category was Avengers, and she was electrifying as “Fat Thor”.

The beauty of Halloween is it’s a day where a person can be anyone or anything. For this year's holiday, Witney Carson’s two boys dressed up as Spider-Man and Captain America, and the DWTS pro opted for the Avengers: Endgame iteration of Chris Hemsworth's God of Thunder, who's best known as “Fat Thor” by fans. Check out the amazing costume reveal:

A post shared by Witney Carson McAllister (@witneycarson)

This is so good! In general, it's also so funny and clever for her to channel the version Thor who has let himself go and lost his abs following defeat at the hands of Thanos. I mean, she essentially found the perfect hack for walking around her neighborhood with her kids while in PJs and a robe while six months pregnant, and matching with them. And, by the looks of it, fans are loving it. Just check out these comments:

It seems that as a pregnancy costume, “Fat Thor” has been quite popular as of late, and I love to see it. Funny enough, Hemsworth actually previously said that putting on the fat suit for Endgame actually helped him understand his own wife’s pregnancies better. When the Australian actor wore the suit during the film shoot, people would apparently come up to him and rub his stomach.

Elsewhere, this Halloween has had the likes of JLo going as Barbarella and Zendaya completely channelling Halle Berry, but it’s hard to top how these Avengers Assemble! Here’s another post of the Carson McAllister family all together on their last Halloween before they become a party of five (due to another baby boy arriving) in a few months:

A post shared by Witney Carson McAllister (@witneycarson)

As someone who loves a DIY costume, I find it especially great how attainable this group costume is and can appreciate that it’s also comfy and cozy for everyone involved. I never would have thought about it when Avengers: Endgame came out, but how cool is it that Thor has inspired pregnant women like Witney Carson to perfectly fit into an Avengers lineup with their family without having to wear a skin-tight suit?

While we don’t expect to see Witney Carson much in the rest of DWTS Season 35, new episodes air every Tuesday night at 8 p.m. ET (with the exception of this week’s airing on Monday). They are available to stream live and catch on demand with a Disney+ subscription.

#3752. New Port Of NFS Underground 2 Turns The Beloved PS2 Racer Into A Wild MMO

It’s a day ending in the letter “Y,” so you know what that means? Yup, another classic video game has been ported in some oddball way with the assistance of AI coding. This time around, someone has gotten PlayStation 2 classic Need for Speed: Underground 2 playable via a web browser, and in this version, you can race alongside dozens of other people at the same time.

Need for Speed: Underground 2 was released back in 2004 and became one of the most popular games of the year thanks to its open-world design and Fast and Furious-like nighttime racing action. It’s like a proto-Forza Horizon, but with a lot more underglow and NOS. And now, thanks to NFS Underground 2 Revived, if you have nostalgic memories of Underground 2 and want to once again drift around its city streets, you can do so in your web browser without having to download a single file or install anything. Oh, and if you want, you can now relive your nostalgia alongside some of the thousands of players currently enjoying this Underground 2 port, according to the site’s data. Just be prepared for some chaos.

My favorite childhood racing game got imported to a website and now 3000 people are free roaming.. this is so fucking funny pic.twitter.com/cUCiz6JDRm

NFSU2 Revived was released late last month, but has recently blown up as fans have discovered the free-to-play browser port via viral clips of the dozens of player-controlled cars smashing into each other on streets that were never designed for this kind of online multiplayer mayhem.Â  Don’t worry, you don’t have to race with others if you just want to enjoy the original solo experience of NSFU2 on your PC in 2026. The multiplayer chaos is opt-in.

The person behind this port claims that they used to play Underground 2 when they were younger, and the creator put this project together so they could “play together again.”

“It worked surprisingly well, and it got a bit out of hand,” said the fan modder and developer. “It’s great to see so many people playing it.”

And as mentioned up top, yes, this port was developed with the help of AI tools, as documented on the Revived’s GitHub page. While I’m not a fan of the AI enshittifcation of the world, it’s also getting harder and harder to play or report on cool game projects and retro mods, like Revived, without running into some amount of AI coding. I’ve talked to numerous devs, big and small, working on these kinds of projects, and for many, these tools are just part of their workflow now.

With a strong sensor, decent specs, and a smart hot-swappable battery system, I like pretty much everything about the MC7 other than the mouse itself, which is ugly, unwieldy, and not as comfortable as I'd like.

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

I must admit, I was mighty intrigued by the idea of a modern mouse (and all their high DPI machinations) with a screen slapped on the side, but I must also admit I thought we would be over the growing pains by now, what with screens being slammed into everything from cases to coolers to controllers.

Yet one look at the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 suggests those growing pains are still being suffered. And using the mouse only confirms it.

But I get the idea in concept. I'm a big fan of my Stream Deck, and find myself regularly using its many controls. Being able to shove those into the side of the mouse with clarity to read what they're doing is intriguing. It's also particularly effective when it comes to swapping DPI, polling rate, and even checking the battery. Those are things that do benefit from a visual component. And yet a few weeks with the MC7 have convinced me I won't be making the swap full time.

✅ You gotta have a large screen on your mouse: As far as I can see, this is the only gaming mouse with modern specs and a big screen from a reputable brand out there.

❌ You want a mouse for competitive gaming: The MC7 is simply not comfortable nor snappy enough for competitive gaming❌ You don't need a large screen on your mouse: We've seen small OLED screens from the likes of SteelSeries and CoolerMaster if you're simply looking for something to display figures.

With a strong sensor, decent specs, and a smart hot-swappable battery system, I like pretty much everything about the MC7 other than the mouse itself, which is ugly, unwieldy, and not as comfortable as I'd like.

Wired and wireless (2.4 GHz and Bluetooth)

Internally, the MC7 has impressive stats. Its Owl-Eye Optical sensor goes all the way up to a max DPI of 30,000, and the polling rate of 8,000 Hz is competitive-level. That's so high, in fact, that the average person won't even see the benefit of it.

And the elephant in the room here: the 2.25-inch colour display is touch-sensitive too, which means you can flick through a couple of different screens depending on your use case. We have seen screens on gaming mice before, like the Cooler Master MM830 and SteelSeries Rival 710 (neither of which are touch screens), but as far as I can tell, the MC7 is the largest on a modern gaming mouse from a reputable brand. That makes it an oddity at the least.

But that's not all the MC7 has going for it. The 4D scroll wheel means you can go up, down, left and right on a page with just the wheel, and you have extra buttons here, too. You have one at the bottom of the thumb rest, another next to the mouse wheel, plus two on the left-hand side, as well as your standard clicks.

It's a wireless mouse, so it comes with a 2.4 GHz receiver, and it also has hot-swappable batteries. The battery charger has a spare USB Type-A port, which means your charger can also be the receiver. This is a sweet system, which makes the MC7 feel like it has infinite battery (as long as you are willing to spend twenty seconds swapping the battery every 10 or so hours).

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

The Owl-Eye sensor is great. It's consistent and smooth, and never posed any problems in any of the games I threw this mouse at. For everyday gaming, I don't have any complaints about how its internals performed. It's a slightly customised version of the PixArt PAW3950 sensor, and will be familiar to anyone who's used the Razer Deathadder V3 Pro, which previously had the exclusive use of PixArt's 30K sensor.

The mouse clicks are a tad loud for my liking, but they're plenty snappy. This bad boy is fitted with Titan Optical switches, and they are perfect under my fingertips. I have yet to hit a single double-click and find them to be very responsive.

However, the biggest problem with performance is how the MC7's weight is balanced and how it feels under the palms. At 135 g grams, it's a fairly heavy mouse (more so than the recent Naga V3 Pro and its mountain of buttons), but this wouldn't be too big of a problem if it could balance that weight in a comfortable way.

However, it feels clunky, and even has a slight rattle at high speeds. This all contributes to a mouse that feels a little lacking in competitive play, even though it's got the internal chops to handle everything on paper.

In use, the screen is rather peculiar. Via the Turtle Beach Swarm II software, you can flit between a few screens, which you customise with your own controls, and they are fairly snappy and responsive. However, having to arch my fingers to actually click on the screen means it's not intended for quick play. That makes it better as a micro function, or a way of displaying battery (but the device's lighting can already indicate battery life and DPI setting). It can display things like health and ammo in Counter-Strike 2, but its viewing angles are pretty poor, meaning it doesn't offer much of a tactical advantage.

The MC7 comes with two 1000 mAh batteries, both of which are hot-swappable. They connect to a charger (which also has a USB port for your 2.4 GHz connector), and this means you technically only need one USB to do everything for your mouse. It's a great system.

To swap the batteries out, you simply take off a compartment where your palm rests, pull the battery out and put a new one in. The MC7's onboard battery is just big enough that I've never noticed the device dying while I'm changing batteries. It's pretty sweet, and with a little practice, it can be swapped in seconds. It's not quite as quick to swap as the Glorious Model O Eternal, with its open battery system, but it is a bit tidier.

Working on my PC every day, then gaming most nights, I found myself swapping out the battery every few days at 1,000 Hz polling, which is perfectly solid given how convenient swapping the batteries is.

The MC7 is a very confusing mouse in regard to its ergonomics. The groove on the left-hand side for your thumb is comfortable and intuitive, yet the two buttons on either side of that groove are awkward to get to. My left thumb buttons on a mouse tend to be going forward and backwards on a page, and therefore I like to have instant access to them. I don't have that access here, and have to physically bend my thumb or extend it to get to each button. The groove also has a texture to it, which is clearly designed so the mouse doesn't slip, and that's also quite strange, as it feels like you aren't encouraged to move your thumb, and yet you have to in order to hit those two buttons.

The back of the mouse curves to my palm well, but the two mouse click buttons are quite curved in the centre. That means, if I hold my hand on the bottom of the mouse, there's air underneath the bottom of my fingers as I hold it, and if I put my palm forward, then there's air underneath my knuckles. I feel like, no matter what way I hold the mouse, I'm holding it just a little wrong.

That's before getting to the screen, a panel that is too long to use all of it while on the go, and close enough to my fingers that I constantly change my DPI whenever I take my hand off the mouse and put it back on again. Perhaps the strangest element of this is that I couldn't seem to figure out a way to lock the screen, which would really make it much better for gaming.

For quickly changing a song or pausing a video, I actually found myself taking my left finger off the left click and wrapping it around the display instead. As far as I can tell, there just isn't a quick and comfortable way to get to all parts of the screen with ease, and I have quite large hands too.

As far as build quality is concerned, the MC7 doesn't feel cheap under the palm, though I'm not a fan of the vibration you get when you click the screen. It just has a hollow feel and sound. The texture on the mouse is cool to the fingertips, and it handles fingerprints well. Despite the fact that you have to take the back cover off to pop the batteries in, I could never get it to come off accidentally either, which is always a plus.

There is a slight rattle if you pick up the mouse and shake it, and that rattle appears to be coming from the 4D mouse wheel. Generally, you don't tend to shake mice, but if you pick it up quickly to move it from one side of the mousepad to the other, it does produce the rattling sound.

One thing I do quite like is a button sunken into the left thumbgrip. I can hold that down and move the rather great-feeling scroll wheel to change volume in an instant, and this is handier and quicker than using the touch screen's volume icons.

The MC7 is clearly intended to fit in alongside the likes of the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II with its combination of copper and black, but it doesn't have the sleekness of its headset counterpart. Instead, it's more Cronenbergian, a collection of skewed angles and bumps, like the tech parts inside its shell are clamouring to get out and your hand is the thing holding them in. It's almost like two separate gaming mice have accidentally stepped inside the teleporter and what has come out is a wretched combination of both.

The right-hand side is relatively low to the ground and with little detailing, whereas the left side is angular, sharp and tall. This is naturally so tall because there's a screen slapped on the side, but it means the entire mouse has a slant going to the right.

Despite this slant, the front is cut at quite a sharp angle too. The MC7 is kind of curvy, and kind of not. It's kind of angular, and also kind of not. It's a hard shape to make sense of and, to my eyes, pretty darn ugly on top of my desk.

One element I do like about the MC7's aesthetic is its choice of RGB. You get a sleek line of it just underneath the mouse, which is customizable, but it glows red when the battery is low, which is a good reminder when I've needed it. The screen also alerts you when your battery is low.

As far as the display is concerned, it has colour, which is a nice touch, but also has weirdly poor viewing angles. If I look at the screen from the position I'd usually game from, it can look washed out. It never looks so washed out that I can't roughly guess what its icons are (and with time, you learn their position anyway), but it makes it feel less quality than the black and copper might suggest.

For the first few weeks with this mouse, I found Turtle Beach's Swarm II to be a mostly fine bit of software, though it could be a little slow. However, this week, the latest update, Software version 1.0.0.63 (which launched on November 2), has seemingly entirely broken on my PC. I can't get it to open, though it remains open in Task Manager. Given it only just launched, I could see this issue being fixed quickly, but it's a shame that so much software for hardware is not consistent.

It is also a necessary bit of software if you would like to customise the screen. With it downloaded, the screen is customizable much like a Stream Deck. Grab widgets from within the app, the mouse's onboard memory, or third-party apps, slap them on the screen, and now you have a new shortcut. Without it, there's not much you can do.

And, as far as I can tell, you can't set totally custom controls, as you can do with the Stream Deck, which limits your customisation a tad. But it's still pretty broad for the most part, and I've rarely found myself looking for a shortcut and not been able to find it.

$160 is a lot of cash for a gaming mouse. It's so much money, in fact, that you can pick up the best gaming mouse out there, the Razer Viper V4 Pro, with its impeccable sensor, great battery life, and lightweight feel, for the same price.

As such, you can pick an overall better, lighter mouse for the same price, or go for the screen. The battery system is certainly neat, though there are other mice out there with hot-swappable batteries.

The MC7 doesn't detract from day-to-day gaming, but I'd much prefer a lower base polling rate if it meant a cheaper price point, as this isn't exactly a competitive-level mouse in function.

It is clear where the budget for this build goes. A large screen couldn't be cheap; the material feels good on the fingertips, and that's before mentioning the research and development costs associated with getting a touchscreen on a mouse. However, it's so much money that, to my palms, it only really feels like the first step for Turtle Beach. It's like a test run of what a touchscreen could be like, and for this price, I don't quite see the vision.

3. Best budget wireless: Mchose G3 V2 Pro

4. Best budget wired: Glorious Model O Eternal

5. Best competitive:Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike

6. Best lightweight: Corsair Sabre V2 Pro

7. Best MMO: Corsair Scimitar Elite Wireless SE

With a strong sensor, decent specs, and a smart hot-swappable battery system, I like pretty much everything about the MC7 other than the mouse itself, which is ugly, unwieldy, and not as comfortable as I'd like.

In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs.

#3749. Footage of a Persona 1 remake has seemingly leaked online

Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online.

The clip, which seemingly gives the remake the subtitle Be Your True Mind, was shared on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit. It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake".

Interestingly, the footage looks a lot like Atlus' more recent entries. It shows off stylish menus and a brief look at combat that closely resembles Persona 5 and Persona 3 Reload. There's also a short social link cutscene in a noticeably different, almost graphic novel art style.

Fans digging through the clip believe they have spotted several details that lend it credibility. These include what looks like Unreal Engine debug text in the top left corner during battle (Atlus switched to Unreal Engine for Persona 3 Reload), a new remix of the original PlayStation game's Pandora theme, and the protagonist being referred to as "Boy With Earring", which is how he is named in Persona 2: Eternal Punishment.

Atlus has not announced a Persona 1 remake, and we can't verify the footage, so treat all of this with the usual caveats.

How do you solve a problem like Persona 4? At Gamescom, we sat down with series director Kazuhisa Wada to talk about the Persona 4 Remake, and ask about how Atlus is approaching the original text for the remake.

#3748. Overwatch’s Director Explains Why The Same Few Heroes Keep Getting Skins

The distribution of cosmetic skinsâwhich heroes get the lionâs share and which ones get significantly fewerâ is a pretty sensitive subject in the Overwatch community. Years of Mercy, Kiriko, and Juno players constantly eating good while Baptiste, Venture, and Wrecking Ball players wait months if not years for a new Legendary skin have some people jaded about the whole process, with some players even criticizing some of the gameâs base hero designs as feeling like they are made with a âcosmetics-firstâ mindset.

During a group interview Kotaku was present for, game director Aaron Keller talked about the challenges of giving attention to its soon-to-be 55 heroes in not just cosmetics, but in storylines the game has introduced over the gameâs 10 years. He says itâs a problem the team at Blizzard has been dealing with for years, one which he admits is âtrickyâ as the roster grows.

âEvery new piece of content that we introduce to the game, whether it’s a hero or even a map, you know, means that the pool of everything that we’ve got, it is spread out a little bit,â he says. âWe recognize how important it is to continue supporting all of the different heroes in the game. And on one side of it, it’s cosmetics, but as we delve into the story and the narrative for the game, you hear from a lot of players about like, âHey, when is this particular hero going to enter the story?â Or, âIt felt like you kind of left off, let’s say, for example, the story of Zarya years ago. When are you going to pick that thing back up?â And so it definitely makes that more difficult.â

With the introduction of the battle pass and frequent store refreshes, Overwatch is producing more skins in recent years than it used to when the game was primarily supported through loot boxes. Keller says that while the team has to prioritize characters who âsupport the actual bottom-line business,â he hopes that initiatives like creating two customizable Mythic skins per season can allow them to more frequently support heroes that have gotten less love over the years, while also always featuring at least one who typically drives skin sales.

âAs a team we have been, over the past few years, constantly expanding our capacity and our throughput for the amount of skins that we make. And as we do that, it allows us to not just make skins for a lot of the heroes that, if I’m being honest, do more to support the actual bottom-line business for the game,â Keller says. âAnd it also allows us to start making cosmetics for some of our other heroes. The place that you can see that the most transparently is the Mythic skins that we release. Each season we release two Mythic skins, and typically one of those is going to be for a hero that we think is actually going to really drive a lot of that support for the business. And then another one is going to be for a hero that typically hasn’t gotten either a Mythic or a lot of other skins in the recent past. So we recognize it’s important to players. We want to be doing as much of it as we can, but we still always want to be doing it in a way that’s also responsible, and [lets us] know that we can continue supporting this game going forward.â

Overwatch started putting out two Mythic skins per season a year ago in October of 2025, and Iâd say most of the seasons that have followed have adhered to the blueprint Keller describes, featuring one hero who is a tried-and-true seller of skins and another one whoâs gotten less love over the years. Lifeweaver and Junkrat are a good example of a pair of heroes who are on opposite ends of the skin-receiving spectrum, but you also have last season when Genji and Widowmaker both got their second Mythic skins in the same batch, a move which frustrated many players who were waiting for an underserved hero to get the spotlight. The current season, which began on October 6, launched with a Mythic skin for Wuyang, who has received several skins since his launch last year. Weâll see what the second Mythic is when the gameâs midseason phase begins later this week.
